This was originally published in TechScape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives. Sign up to receive it here .
Hello, and welcome to TechScape. I’m your host, Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you from a plane back from Web Summit in Lisbon. Today in tech, we’re discussing the implications of Jensen Huang’s ouster, and the recent spate of failures in critical infrastructure in everything from Microsoft Outlook accounts to air traffic control to copper wires in routers.
The chief executive officer of what once was the most valuable company in the world resigned on Thursday. Jensen Huang ’s departure from chipmaker Nvidia after news broke he had at least three affairs – one with an executive at the datacenter firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence has investigated for spying for China; others with his own employees – has already cost his company hundreds of billions in stock market value. It may cost the world economy much more. Nvidia is central to the AI boom both as chipmaker and lender.
We’ll know more about the company’s path forward later on Tuesday when it reports its quarterly earnings. Executives, especially interim CEO Colette Kress, will face investors’ questions about the post-Huang era.
The scandal has highlighted divisions among two heavyweights within the Trump administration, each fighting for the US to take their preferred stance toward China. The treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, is accusing the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick , of failing to curb sales by Nvidia that contravened export controls.
Here’s how the business of Megaspeed worked, which is what the two secretaries are warring over. Nvidia is barred from selling advanced chips to China. Megaspeed, where alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang worked, would buy Nvidia chips from its base in south-east Asia, installing them in datacenters in Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. From there, it would lease or sell them to Chinese clients.
Lutnick has pushed to allow more trade with China, particularly where his family business, Cantor Fitzgerald, is concerned . Bessent argues for a more hawkish posture and more restrictions.
The question is what will happen next. I think the scandal will result in harsher export controls on China , given that Megaspeed facilitated about $12bn in chip sales in contravention of US export controls. Monday morning already saw the Trump administration moving to tighten them.
Who’s going to win? Both men are traveling with Donald Trump to China this week. I’ll be listening to the president’s remarks for clues about which policy path he’ll choose.
Had Jensen Huang amassed too much influence before his downfall? The Nvidia founder seemed indispensable to the success of his company until the very moment he left.
Elon Musk and a host of other Silicon Valley power players argued over the weekend that Huang was irreplaceable and that he should be reinstated. Trump said the same thing on Monday: “He could return. There’s a big group of ‌people that would like him to return … I would certainly not mind seeing that.” They’re certainly right that it will be difficult to find another businessman like him.
The possibility may be remote. The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Huang had discussed a return to Nvidia with allies, à la Sam Altman’s firing and rehiring at OpenAI. The next day, the FT reported that Nvidia’s board of directors was not considering reinstating Huang.
Critics of Silicon see Huang’s departure as a repudiation of the myth of the all-knowing, all-important company founder.
“This week is seeing a long overdue reckoning for the genius-founder business model,” said Alison Taylor, associate professor at New York University’s business school. Gil Durán , a strident critic of Silicon Valley, made a similar point during a panel organized in response to the news, as did Carissa Véliz, a philosophy professor at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI.
Nvidia’s fate is the highest-profile example I’ve ever seen of “ key man risk ”. Companies heavily reliant on the brilliance of one person – usually a man – or a small group of executives often notify their investors that, if said vital person goes out of commission, the business will suffer. Companies with more diffuse responsibility hedge against that possibility but become more bureaucratic, leading many Silicon Valley companies to operate with as few employees as necessary for as long as possible.
“Relying on the judgment and ethics of one person, no matter how brilliant, is always a catastrophically bad idea, and powerful CEOs are particularly vulnerable because they tend to be surrounded by people that only say yes to them,” Taylor said.
Huang had made no succession plan to speak of, though that may be a failure of Nvidia’s board as much as his own. Huang reportedly managed about 60 people, meaning there are not likely successors who have ascended through the ranks. Judging by Nvidia’s stock price, this approach to management worked until the key man himself hit a crisis.
Cast in another light, though, Huang’s tenure looks like the best case of a founder assuming the role of longtime CEO. He presided over Nvidia for more than 30 years, and shepherded it from gaming chip company to vital cryptocurrency supplier to the keystone of the AI boom. Its wares are considered the cream of the crop, so incomparable that they are the target of international espionage operations and so valuable that the company forecast $100bn in quarterly revenue .

A spate of failures indicates critical systems are crumbling as we speak, particularly in the US. Banks, planes, email accounts and boats all crashing – it feels like nothing is working and everything is broken.
Late last week, an outage of Microsoft Outlook started that would balloon into millions having no access to their email or other critical services. Jails could not release prisoners, hospitals turned to paper records, schools lost contact with parents, and police departments could not receive crime reports. Microsoft said it had resolved the issue and restored service by Saturday. It also issued an apology. The company did not attribute the blackout to a cybersecurity breach, instead saying in an initial report that a combination of a months-old bug, malfunctioning internal connections and insufficient server capacity sparked the outage.
The day after the Microsoft outage began, the US Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights across the country because of a malfunctioning communication system. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy attributed the stoppage to “a contractor doing routine maintenance to switch telecommunication lines from old copper wire … to fiber”. The FAA, he said on Saturday, was still working to determine whether the fault was “incompetence” by the contractor, or “a faulty router”.
Copper wires downing all US flights in the year 2026, when we have thousands of self-driving cars on the roads and rockets landing in giant machine arms ? The discrepancy gives credence to the axiom by the author William Gibson: “The future is already here – it’s just not evenly distributed.”
Also on Friday, an oil tanker collided with a passenger cruise on the Mississippi River. Mercifully, no one was killed . On Sunday, Australian students couldn’t take their final exams because of a tech failure . On Monday, leading US banks reported big outages, primarily JPMorgan Chase. Customers could not access online services such as Zelle, which the bank attributed to an unspecified technical issue. The same day, multiple main airlines reported major outages. Sinema dünyasının yıllardır merakla beklediği yeni James Bond 'un kim olacağı sorusu yanıt buldu. Amazon MGM Studios, efsanevi 007 karakterini İngiliz oyuncu Robert Pattinson'ın canlandıracağını duyurdu. Alacakaranlık ve The Batman filmleriyle dünya çapında ün kazanan 40 yaşındaki oyuncu, Daniel Craig'den boşalan koltuğun yeni sahibi oldu.
2021 yapımı Ölmek İçin Zaman Yok filmiyle Daniel Craig'in James Bond macerasının sona ermesinin ardından gözler yeni oyuncunun kim olacağına çevrilmişti. Uzun süren oyuncu seçme sürecinin sonunda yapım şirketi tercihini Robert Pattinson'dan yana kullandı.
Pattinson böylece Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan ve Daniel Craig'in ardından James Bond'u canlandıracak yedinci oyuncu oldu.
Yeni rolüne ilişkin açıklama yapan Robert Pattinson, James Bond'un sinema tarihinin en efsanevi karakterlerinden biri olduğunu belirterek 007 rolünün kendisine emanet edilmesini hayatının en büyük onurlarından biri olarak nitelendirdi.

Heads up, radio and TV programming will be briefly interrupted this afternoon.
Radio and TV broadcasts will be interrupted for about one minute at 2:20PM ET on Tuesday while FEMA and the FCC test the country’s Emergency Alert System. Unlike recent communications outages , this is a planned interruption that FEMA is required to run every three years. FEMA says today’s test includes radio and television broadcasters, cable systems, satellite radio and television providers, and wireline video providers. This test doesn’t include phones.
You’ll hear high-pitched alert tones and the following test message:
“This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is only a test. No action is required by the public.”
Radio and TV programming will continue as usual after the test wraps up. FEMA runs tests like this when there’s not an actual emergency so it can find technical and operational issues with the Emergency Alert System. If there is a real emergency or severe weather event today, the test will run on December 3rd instead.

Amazon no longer considers the midrange Fire TV Stick 4K Plus as part of its official lineup following the launch of it latest Fire TV Stick 4K, but that doesn’t mean the streaming device isn’t still good value. It does require a separate power adapter, though, whereas the newer model can draw power directly from your TV’s USB port. Thanks to Alexa Plus support, you can also press the voice button on the included Alexa Voice Remote to find something to watch, control compatible smart home devices like lights and thermostats, check sports scores, and more without getting off your couch. Just don’t expect a customizable shortcut button, as that’s exclusive to the latest Fire TV Remote.
One final note: the Plus ships with Amazon’s Fire OS, and unlike the company’s Vega OS that ships in newer streaming sticks, the former allow for sideloading of Android TV apps, if that’s of interest to you.

Science Corporation , the medical technology start-up founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak in 2021, raised a $400 million Series D, the company said in a blog post .
Investors in the new round valued the company at $3.5 billion, a person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch. Those backers included Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator, and PLC Neurotech.
Hodak, who talked his way into a graduate neuroscience lab as a college student and has pursued biotechnology ever since, co-founded Science to leverage new technologies to understand and interact with the brain.
Science’s first product is PRIMA, a wearable and implantable chip that helps people with age-related macular degeneration recover some vision. The device is approved in Europe and available in Germany, as well as being trialled for new conditions.
Hodak announced that the device is now being trialled for patients with another blindness-causing condition, Stargardt’s disease, while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
With the funding, the company aims to bring the device to the United States through the FDA’s Humanitarian Device Exemption, which lets experimental medical technology be used to treat rare conditions. Science has convinced the FDA that advanced macular degeneration in both eyes is uncommon enough to let them seek approval to use the device on people in the US.
Still, the startup’s big ambition and founding purpose is connecting directly to the human brain through a bio-hybrid sensor built from a combination of cultured neurons and silicon. The company is currently designing initial human trials of the device with Yale neurosurgery professor Murat Günel, who told TechCrunch it could offer potential treatments for Parkinson’s disease, among other brain injuries and illnesses.

Nvidia has formed a committee to oversee national security policies and export control compliance following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who had links to one of the company’s customers.
Nvidia said Tuesday that the new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. The move comes amid increased scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Huang’s alleged ties to the suspected spy and his advocacy for easing restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China.
The Commerce Department said Monday it was planning to introduce new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside of the U.S. in an effort to prevent companies in China and elsewhere from circumventing existing rules by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. The interim rule was made in direct response to the unfolding chip smuggling scandal at Nvidia.
The announcement comes just a few hours before Nvidia’s highly anticipated third-quarter earnings call. Analysts, the media, and shareholders expect the company to address the controversy and outline how it might affect operations. This is the first major action by the company under the leadership of Collette Kress, the company’s CFO who took over as interim CEO after Huang stepped down last week.
The committee, which will meet at least quarterly, will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and include fellow directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members.
Nvidia already has a national security team and global trade compliance team. Those teams will now report to this board committee and Kress on day-to-day operations.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress later this month.

I retested the base Surface Laptop, and Microsoft’s optimizations seem to be working.
As recently as the beginning of the year, 16GB of RAM was common on sub-$800 Windows laptops, which helped compensate for an increasingly bloated-feeling Windows 11 . But with the cost of RAM skyrocketing this year, 8GB is once again typical for a starting configuration. The MacBook Neo got away with it, but Windows laptops, including Microsoft’s own 13-inch Surface Laptop , could struggle. Microsoft was talking a big game about making Windows faster and more reliable before the RAM crisis really hit , and it now seems like that effort is beginning to bear fruit .
Earlier this month , Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft’s EVP of Windows and devices, detailed in a blog post the improvements the company has made to Windows 11 to address the constraints of 8GB PCs. In it, Davuluri claims, “Windows is now up to 20% more responsive, and multitasking is up to 40% faster in our lab test.”
The most significant change is in memory management. When there isn’t enough available memory to handle all active data, some of it has to be offloaded (or “paged out”) to storage. And SSDs, especially in lower-cost laptops, are much slower than RAM.
When Windows needs to access data that’s been paged out from the RAM to the SSD, it’s called a hard fault (or page fault). If it happens a lot — say, on a laptop with only 8GB of RAM — it leads to little slowdowns like browser tabs requiring a refresh before you can access them again. Davuluri says, “Windows can now keep up to 2 GB more of your active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, so an app or tab you left open is less likely to reload when you return.”
To test this, I fired up the same 13-inch Surface Laptop with 8GB of RAM that I reviewed back in July, when I proclaimed eight is not enough for Windows. This laptop was one of the worst examples of RAMageddon’s current stranglehold on computing: With half the RAM of last year’s base model , it struggled to keep up with my regular workload. And this is Microsoft’s hardware.
Before updating the Surface to the latest Windows 11 build, I got reacquainted with this laptop and the version of Windows I left it on (25H2, build 26200.8875). It was rough. Running about 20 tabs (on the latest Chrome build) while streaming a 4K YouTube video and using Slack and Signal made everything from clicking tabs to swiping around Windows with trackpad gestures feel sluggish. Chrome tabs and apps would refresh after leaving them in the background for just a short moment. When you’re multitasking and bouncing between many tabs, like when researching something, those refreshes get incredibly frustrating. And the fan was running audibly the whole time. Keeping the Resource Monitor open showed memory hard faults ranging from just under 700 faults per second to 29,000 faults per second, during which Windows ground to a halt. Seeing this number literally go off its chart showed just how badly Windows 11 struggled with memory management on 8GB before the update.
Now, after updating the Surface Laptop to Windows 11 version 26H2, build 26300.9974 ( memory improvements are live on build 26300.9818 and beyond) things are much improved. I opened over 30 Chrome tabs while streaming the same 4K YouTube video and running the same chat apps, and Windows slowed a bit, but nowhere near as much. I could feel things like Task View get a little less responsive and at times stuttery, but it was the way you’d expect when taxing a system. Chrome tabs required less frequent refreshes. The fan also took longer to kick in and ran a little quieter and for shorter durations when it did.
Taking a fresh look at the Resource Monitor, hard faults at normal operation were now under 300 per second, with occasional jumps to about 1,000. Performance was even slightly better when I subbed out Chrome for Microsoft Edge. Edge felt more responsive under load and had fewer hard faults when running 30 tabs, the same 4K YouTube video, and a Google Meet video call.
I’m happy to see that the 8GB Surface Laptop now performs better, and I’m equally relieved that Windows 11 is starting to feel more viable on 8GB of RAM. (It’s still a shame the 8GB Surface Laptop costs more than last year’s 16GB, but I digress.) Do I want 8GB of RAM in any laptop I’m personally buying? No.
As I said when I reviewed the latest Dell XPS 13 , I appreciate that 8GB is workable — and it should be fine for basic needs today — but I still advise getting 16GB if you’re able. The extra headroom will keep things speedy for longer, especially after you bog a computer down with lots of files, apps, or games. And as much better as the 8GB Surface Laptop is now, I still managed to crash Chrome entirely with fewer than three dozen tabs. Microsoft has done better by its entry-level laptop, but it’s not a miracle worker.
Our ongoing RAMageddon makes living with lower quantities of memory a grim reality. Microsoft is partly to blame for that, of course. And it hasn’t done itself any favors with all the feature bloat it put into Windows 11 during the Copilot / AI era . Meanwhile, other OSes, like Linux, macOS, and ChromeOS, can get by better with less. Still, I’m glad to see Microsoft ever so slightly right the ship in this one way.

Music legend is joined by Jimmy Barnes and Peter Garrett in backing Not AI’s To Take campaign ahead of Aria awards
Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast
Australia’s creative community has launched a major campaign pleading with the Albanese government not to water down copyright law amid furious lobbying from AI companies, ahead of Wednesday night’s Aria awards .
Music legends Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett are among those backing the Not AI’s To Take campaign, supported by dozens of creative groups representing the recording, writing, publishing, film, television and media industries.
While the government maintains it will not undermine copyright law, the industry minister, Tim Ayres, said on Tuesday “the status quo is no good” for the creative sector, ahead of a package of AI legislation expected by early 2027.
But creatives have pushed back on such claims, arguing copyright law doesn’t need updating – just better enforcement, and that changes could put the $70bn creative industry and its 600,000 workers at risk.
“[AI platforms] haven’t made one phone call yet. They haven’t called us. They haven’t called anybody,” said Dean Ormston, CEO of music rights organisation Apra Amcos.
“There’s nothing wrong with the copyright framework. The problem is getting somebody to sit at the table and have a discussion with us.”
Not AI’s To Take is backed by the likes of Aria, the Copyright Agency, the Australian Directors’ Guild, Screen Producers Australia, the Australian Society of Authors, the Australian Writers’ Guild, and media organisations including Foxtel, Free TV, Nine, Seven and Guardian Australia.
Australian musicians including Montaigne and KLP have backed the campaign online, while Guardian Australia understands Barnes, Kelly and Garrett – some of Anthony Albanese’s favourite musicians – will also feature.
“Our government has been a huge supporter of Australian music and creativity, and now we’re asking them to continue that support by standing firm on copyright and making sure big tech doesn’t get to rewrite the rules at the expense of creators,” said KLP, real name Kristy Lee Peters.
In quotes shared on the campaign’s website, Barnes said: “I think that these companies should go and f..k themselves.”
Kelly is quoted as saying: “Australia has had some of the best copyright laws, something to be proud of. Now is the time for our government to show some backbone.”
Although Albanese has declared it would be “theft” if creatives weren’t paid for their work, some AI companies have argued it is too difficult to make individual licensing deals under existing copyright law. AI companies have said they need legal certainty on the copyright issue before investing and training models in Australia, with Anthropic putting forward an “opt-out” model to scrape creative works unless a rightsholder objected.
However Anthropic told a Senate committee it would “provide ongoing access to frontier models to eligible Australian entities, regardless of whether training is permitted.”
The government is expected to unveil a long-awaited legislative package on AI in late 2026 or early 2027, with proposals around datacentres, online safety, productivity and copyright. Albanese said last week that artists “need to be compensated if their work is used”. But the creative community is concerned that lobbying from big tech may sway government decisions.
“This isn’t a smear campaign. We’re just making some noise out in the open, where tech companies are doing it in the shadows,” said Patrizia Di Biase-Dyson, CEO of the Australian Publishers Association.
“Everything is at stake. We have to do as much as possible to educate everyone.”
Ormston said creative industries welcomed the investment and opportunities of AI, and had applauded both Labor’s rebuffing of a text and data mining exemption and Albanese’s public support. But he said artists were worried about potential changes.
“Our very clear message to the government has been: hold firm. You are absolutely saying the right thing. You are absolutely right in the fact that while we want AI in this country, we want it on Australia’s terms,” Ormston said.
Asked about the campaign on Tuesday, Ayres said “nothing has changed in terms of the government’s approach” to copyright.
“I understand the anxiety, though. For those workers, the status quo is no good for them. Their work is currently being appropriated, today, offshore. We have set out a program for a scheme of legislation that would protect those rights, make sure that artificial intelligence investment in Australia is on Australia’s terms.
“We’re not about undermining copyright here. That commitment has been made so many times now.”
A spokesperson for the attorney general, Michelle Rowland, said the government was “committed to supporting” creatives, and pledged any copyright changes would “deliver meaningful control and fair compensation”.
But independent senator David Pocock urged caution around any moves, warning that copyright changes could create a legal “loophole” to make Australia a global “data laundering hotspot”.
“There are more than 100 court cases on foot involving copyright and AI training in the US and we should wait for these to play out before making any changes given the risks of getting it wrong are so high,” he said.

Siber güvenlik alanında yapay zeka modelleri ve otonom ajanlar geliştiren Corma , 125 milyon dolarlık Seri A yatırım turunu tamamladı. New Enterprise Associates 'ın (NEA) liderlik ettiği yatırım turuna şirketin mevcut yatırımcıları Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures ve Coatue da katıldı.
Yeni yatırımla birlikte Corma'nın değerlemesi 1 milyar dolara ulaştı. Corma'nın bundan yalnızca üç ay önce 60 milyon dolarlık tohum yatırımıyla gizlilik modundan çıktığını hatırlatalım. Son yatırımla beraber şirketin bugüne kadar aldığı toplam yatırım 185 milyon dolara yükseldi.
2025 yılında kurulan ve Tel Aviv ile San Francisco'da faaliyet gösteren Corma, geleneksel genel amaçlı yapay zeka modellerinden farklı olarak savunma odaklı siber güvenlik için eğitilen temel modeller geliştiriyor. Şirket, bu modelleri kurumların güvenlik ekipleriyle birlikte çalışan otonom yapay zeka ajanlarına dönüştürüyor.
Corma'nın yapay zeka ajanları, şirketlerin mevcut güvenlik araçları üzerinden çalışabiliyor. Sistem; güvenlik kayıtları, ağ trafiği, yapılandırmalar ve güvenlik olayları gibi farklı kaynaklardan gelen verileri inceleyerek tehditlerin tespit edilmesi ve güvenlik süreçlerinin yürütülmesi gibi görevleri üstleniyor. Böylece Corma, güvenlik ekiplerinin gerçekleştirdiği bazı karmaşık işleri baştan sona yapay zeka ajanlarına devretmeyi hedefliyor. Şirketin bu alana odaklanmasının temelinde, genel amaçlı yapay zeka modellerinin siber saldırılardaki yeteneklerinin savunma tarafındaki yeteneklerinden daha hızlı geliştiği düşüncesi bulunuyor.
Corma CEO'su ve kurucu ortağı Alon Pluda , kodlama modellerinin açık bulma ve bunlardan yararlanma konusunda giderek daha yetenekli hale geldiğine dikkat çekiyor. Corma ise yapay zekayı özellikle savunma tarafının ihtiyaç duyduğu güvenlik verileri üzerinde eğiterek bu farkı kapatmayı amaçlıyor.
Corma, gizlilik modundan çıkmasının ardından büyük şirketlerden gelen talebin hızla arttığını belirtiyor. Şirket, bu talebi karşılayabilmek amacıyla sunucu kapasitesini üç ay içinde 24 kat artırdı. Corma'nın açıklamasına göre yeni yatırım özellikle temel modellerin ölçeklendirilmesi ve işlem kapasitesinin artırılması için kullanılacak. Şirket ayrıca ekibini de seçici bir şekilde büyütmeyi planlıyor.
Corma'nın kısa sürede 1 milyar dolar değerlemeye ulaşması, yapay zeka ve siber güvenliğin kesişimindeki girişimlere yönelik yatırımcı ilgisinin de bir göstergesi. Wall Street Journal'ın aktardığı verilere göre küresel siber güvenlik girişimlerinde tohum aşamasından Seri B'ye kadar gerçekleşen yatırım anlaşmalarının toplam değeri, 2026 'nın ilk dokuz ayında 4,7 milyar dolara ulaşarak 2025'in tamamındaki yatırım seviyesini geride bıraktı.

Smart glasses company Xreal has released its magnum opus—the Xreal Aura, a $1,279 pair of extended-reality glasses that runs on Google’s Android XR platform. The Aura glasses can project virtual screens into the wearer’s field of vision and include augmented-reality elements for use in the real world.
The Aura glasses arrive just before the first wave of Android XR glasses from Google and Samsung, in partnership with glasses manufacturers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Those devices aim squarely at Meta’s smart-glasses empire. But the Aura glasses are more like virtual reality headsets , now in a more comfortable, glasses-like design. They go head-to-head with Meta’s VR Glasses , slated for release in early 2027.
The first big caveat about the Aura glasses is that they’re wired. A long cord hooks onto the end of one of the glasses’ arms via a USB-C cable. That cord connects to an attached compute puck, about the size of a smartphone and weighing a little more than a half-pound. It comes in 12 or 16 GB storage options and has a battery that powers the glasses for roughly four to five hours with constant use.
When the Aura glasses work, they’re wonderful. The glasses are pretty lightweight, at 95 grams. A four-mic array sits in the arms with Bose EQ tuning that sounds great. (You can also connect wireless headphones.) The display screen has a 1920 x 1200-pixel-per-eye resolution that is noticeably better than other Xreal glasses I’ve worn. A 70-degree field of view means the screens and virtual elements pop up in a wide frame of the wearer’s vision. That means the outer edges of your view will still be the real-life room around you. That can help if you’re trying not to fall over, but it can also be noticeable when trying to feel immersed in a movie.
The big thing about Aura is that you can, in theory, run every app that already exists on Android. Xreal has a few primary categories for how it expects people to use its Aura glasses. The big one is entertainment. Like other Xreal glasses, the Aura can project a screen right in your field of vision. You can watch movies, TV shows, or YouTube videos, right in your field of view. The virtual screen stays fixed, or it can follow you around as you turn your head. You can also unplug the glasses from the compute puck and use them as display glasses to extend your Steam Deck ’s screen, for example, though I had issues with that when playing more graphics-intensive games like Cyberpunk 2077 .
The Aura glasses attach to a compute puck for processing, which also doubles as a battery.
The other big use case is productivity. The Aura glasses can host virtual workstations that let you swap between tabs and keep multiple tasks running. So you can have a Google Doc right in front of you, Spotify to the side, and those Slack messages you keep ignoring in the back. If you’ve ever wished you had even more space to stash all your browser tabs, this is the device for you. Pair it with a Bluetooth keyboard, and you’ll have a whole workstation on your face , even on a plane, without having to crane your neck awkwardly at a laptop. I wrote almost half this review with the glasses as my screen, but eventually swapped back to a regular desktop to give my eyes a rest.
There are also augmented reality experiences, like using Google Earth to turn a room into a 3D model of a city that you can stomp around in like Godzilla, plus immersive virtual tours so you can see exotic places like the Galapagos.
Two lenses are set in the frame, one smaller lens behind the other. The smaller lens carries the display and AR elements, popping them up within a 70-degree field of view. The outer lens can go from perfectly see-through to very dark. Turning up the darkness makes it easier to see the projected virtual screens. Turning the darkness down enables a much clearer pass-through, which can help you avoid tripping over things while walking around.
That said, these glasses aren’t really meant to be worn while walking around. Even with no AR elements enabled, the double-lens layout feels distracting. There is also no way around the fact that these glasses are still pretty chunky. If you can rock the thicc fit, then great, but I’ve gotten some pointed stares when I walk around with them.
The compute puck can be used as a trackpad to navigate the interface, and it also has a fingerprint sensor.
The glasses do feel lightweight, but after a few minutes of use, they start to heat up. When I take them off, they leave red divots on the bridge of my nose. It’s a small price to pay, though, and it doesn’t ruin the experience. Compare that to something like a VR headset, which does offer better immersion but at the cost of being heavy and uncomfortable to wear for long stretches.
The compute puck can be an annoyance. It’s light enough, but using the Aura glasses means you have to carry yet another thing that is strapped to the device on your face. There were some smart choices made on the puck, like a fingerprint sensor for biometric authentication, and the puck’s surface works like a trackpad to move the onscreen cursor. That seems much smoother than reaching out to control the device with hand movements, but the trackpad wasn't very precise either. Which is a shame, as it would be ideal for someone on an airplane, say, who wants to control the device without punching the seat in front of them.
Controls are the biggest problem I’ve had with the Aura. The front cameras track your hand movements. Hold out your hand and pinch two fingers together to open up an app or move a window. It works most of the time, but some gestures don’t always register. I find myself trying to open Spotify or switch between titles on Prime Video and have to repeatedly pinch the air in front of me for anything to happen. When people have been around to see me, they’ve told me I look like I’ve gone bonkers, just grunting and wildly pinching thin air.
The Xreal Aura glasses are a stunning display of how far smart-glasses technology has come. But they still feel like a novelty that most people won’t want or need. They haven’t quite solved the core issues facing the product category—looking like a dork or being effortlessly comfortable to wear. But they do feel like a big step in the right direction. If only they could get a pinch more usable.

As AI-generated slop continues to flood music streaming platforms, Spotify is rolling out an “Artist Profile Protection” tool to all artists, giving them control over the music appearing under their name. The official launch comes eight months after the company began beta testing the feature with select artists.
Spotify says the tool is designed to address a longstanding issue across streaming services, where music can end up on the wrong artist profile due to deliberate impersonation, metadata errors, or shared artist names.
The update comes as Billboard reported last month that Sony Music had requested the removal of more than 260,000 deepfake songs from digital platforms, nearly double the number the label disclosed in March.
With this new feature, Spotify is aiming to give artists more control over their digital identities as the volume of music uploaded to streaming services continues to grow.
Artists can enable the feature through Spotify for Artists to receive alerts when new music is submitted under their name. If a release doesn’t belong to them, they can remove their association with it to stop it from appearing on their profile.
By default, releases go live as scheduled unless an artist intervenes. If artists want greater control, they can choose to switch on an advanced setting that requires them to manually approve or reject releases before they appear on their profile.
“Artists should never have to find someone else’s music under their name, said Sam Duboff. Spotify’s Global Head of Marketing and Policy, in an email, stated to TechCrunch. “Their artist profile should be in their control. Starting today, every artist on Spotify can use Artist Profile Protection to review what shows up on their profile and prevent spammy and incorrect releases from ever reaching their page or their fans. We’re the first and only streaming service with a solution to the industry-wide problem of content mismatch, and we hope it sets a new standard for streaming platforms.”
The company says it worked with thousands of artists during the beta testing phase to refine the tool and make it easier to protect their profiles without disrupting release schedules.

Genesis AI has “cracked dexterous manipulation,” CEO and co-founder Zhou Xian says.
To make his case, Xian hosted TechCrunch at Genesis AI’s Silicon Valley facility, where its physical AI model operated a pair of off-the-shelf robotic arms. In one demo, the arms picked up two small cardboard boxes, scanned them, placed them in a larger cardboard box, folded it closed, taped it shut, and then plucked a label off a strip of printer tape and applied it to the box.
It’s an impressive demo, exactly the kind of complex workflow that today’s robots struggle to complete. And while Genesis wouldn’t let your reporter mess with the robot’s mise en place to test its wiles, the company did agree to re-run the presentation. During the second go-round, the robot fumbled a box and had a heck of a time peeling the tiny adhesive label off the printer tape. A mistake, but also the kind of edge case that can be used to improve a model—”hiccup data,” a Genesis executive suggests.
This is the exact gap —between a lab demo and reliable automation—that Genesis , and the rest of the humanoid physical AI ecosystem, need to bridge if they want to avoid another robot winter. To do so, Xian’s company is announcing a $500 million Series A round led by Khosla Ventures, Premji Invest, and Eclipse.
Xian and Genesis president Théophile Gervet, who met as graduate students in a Carnegie Mellon University lab, cofounded the company in 2024. Genesis announced its $105 million seed round in July 2025. The company’s strategy is vertical integration: generating the bulk of its own training data, developing its own generative AI model, and doing both in concert with the design and construction of a humanoid robot.
“We wanted to ship the best robot, end-to-end product,” Xian said.
The startup’s focus on dexterity — the robot’s ability to do stuff with its hands — and gathering the right data to achieve it sets it apart from competitors like Figure or Agility. Genesis gathers force data (apparently the unlock for effective manipulation) using a sensor-enabled glove. The gloves, and accompanying headset cameras, are worn by more than 100 real workers around the world, whose activities contribute to a training dataset that feeds into the company’s model.
The company’s robots wear the same sensor-equipped gloves, and their “hands” are designed to mimic the proportions of human hands. That fidelity, Xian says, enables the robots’ capabilities in sorting and wire manipulation.
The other big investment the company has made is in simulation. One of its advisers, Minchen Li, is a co-author of an influential physics algorithm used by the startup to create millions of high-fidelity models of the robot’s experience.
Still, about that robot: Xian said that the company’s model was more capable when operating Eno, the company’s flagship humanoid robot. But Eno wasn’t ready to demonstrate its abilities for TechCrunch.
A handsome machine bearing more than a hint of the late Steve Jobs’ influence on tech gadgets and their marketing, Eno reflects “the feeling” the company wants to deliver to its customers. That means less of a Terminator -styled metal skeleton and more of an iMac on wheels.
Genesis said it has built 30 to 40 Enos, but wasn’t ready to share how many it would make in the year ahead. The company would only say that a mass-manufacturing contractor had been chosen to start work next year in the U.S. and that the design of the mass-produced version had been finalized. The company is piloting the machine with a handful of undisclosed customers.
To realize the company’s vision, Xian says the key bottleneck is hardware capability, both in mechanical design and in the supply chains needed to produce industrial-grade machines. Right now, the company’s dexterous hands can only operate for a few weeks of regular work before they need to be replaced.
For truly generalized robotic intelligence, Genesis needs more data. Xian pooh-poohs the finer distinctions between architectures like Vision-Language-Action models and World-Action models . In his view, the software is ultimately transformers and attention, so “what really matters is is the whole infra — the training infrastructure, the data infrastructure, and the quality of the data.” He estimates that “the model architecture contributes to maybe 10% of of the final [result].”
“I don’t think we expect or we need another fundamental scientific leap,” he told TechCrunch. “No, we have all the recipes. It’s just about execution.”

Blow to Kremlin as prestigious bridge linking occupied Ukrainian peninsula struck by missile. Plus, what is in store for Robert Pattinson, the new 007?
Good morning. Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.
Ukraine has declared that the Kerch bridge, built eight years ago after Vladimir Putin’s 2014 annexation of Crimea, is illegal. It has repeatedly attempted to destroy it. The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed that the bridge, which was temporarily closed on Monday, was no longer usable. Photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait.
Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests before the US president’s arrival. Organisers say they expect as many as 10,000 people to join protests against Trump as he attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people, with large parts of the Philippine capital closed off and tight security in place. Some protesters burned effigies of the US president, and demonstrators angry at the cost-of-living and energy shock caused by the Iran war tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center, but were blocked by police.
You can follow developments at the Apec and Asean summits with our live blog .
A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command has said, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East. Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.
The Roosevelt joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian shipping.
Microsoft has identified the root causes of the global outage that crippled Outlook, Exchange and a host of other software last week. An initial report identified three factors: a months-old bug, malfunctioning internal connections, and server capacity. Each of these factors may have easily been resolved on their own but, taken together, led to a major outage that was harder to mitigate, Microsoft executives said.
Cornell University is to announce a “full review” of fraternities and sororities determining their future on campus, after an alleged sexual assault brought scrutiny to the system at the Ivy League school. The university’s president, Michael Kotlikoff, announced the review in an update outlining several steps the institution had taken after a woman said she was gang-raped at an on-campus fraternity’s house. Cornell had already banned fraternity parties for the rest of the academic year.
The US has beaten Canada to win the women’s ice hockey world championship in Denmark, becoming the first US team to capture Olympic and world titles in the same calendar year.
A judge has scheduled Lindsay Clancy ’s second trial in the killings of her three young children for late March , over the objections of prosecutors.
Dolores Huerta has been honored in a ceremony at California’s state capitol.
Authorities investigating a bomb found at an ethanol production plant in Illinois have taken a suspect into custody , according to the mayor there.
California is suing OpenAI , accusing the artificial intelligence company of developing its technology without safety or the public’s interest in mind.
Several companies that received refunds for paying Donald Trump’s tariffs have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers , an investigation has found .
Zohran Mamdani , New York City’s mayor, has announced he is disbanding a city police unit accused of using excessive force.
The oldest known survivor of the Pearl Harbor attack has died aged 106 . Freeman Johnson, a firefighter below the deck during the attack, told the Associated Press in May: “While all the rigamarole was going on topside, I was inside a steam drum. Couldn’t see anything, absolutely nothing.” Only 11 known Pearl Harbor survivors are still living, all of whom are centenarians.
Andrew Pulver writes that the wait for the new Bond is over , but that’s only the beginning – there are still small issues such as the script, title, setting, casting, branding and promotion of the next instalment of the franchise. Nadia Khomami, meanwhile, traces Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to 007.
In a new biography, the maestro of American melancholy is called a “sadist” and a “prize hog” by his wife – who was aghast to see their domestic and bedroom problems surface in his most famous works. Louis Shadwick explains .
Described by Mark Blacklock as “the perfect conspiracy model for consumer capitalist societies”, this is a fascinating read about how a convicted fraudster from North Dakota and a white supremacist inspired the “sovereign citizen” movement. It has blossomed around the world – wasting public resources and ruining lives along the way.
The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, research has found. Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia, meanwhile, have been named as the biggest CO 2 exporters in history in a new analysis of data since 1850.
Follow the latest from Cop31 with Ajit Niranjan on our live blog .
Two months after the discovery of the first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on the US west coast, the eggs have hatched – and California’s first group of 75 native-born olive ridley sea turtles have been released into the Pacific. Hopefully they will thrive better than Fiona the hippo is doing at the moment – she is under veterinary care after eating a hat at Cincinnati zoo.

Yapay zeka destekli CRM yazılımları geliştiren Dreamteam , toplamda 53 milyon dolar yatırım aldı. Şirketin yatırım turu tohum ve A serisi olmak üzere iki aşamada gerçekleşti. ABD merkezli Dreamteam'in tohum yatırım turuna Together Fund , A serisi yatırım turuna ise Accel liderlik etti. Premji Invest de şirketin yatırım turlarına katılan yatırımcılar arasında yer aldı.
Şirket, yeni yatırımı CRM platformunu geliştirmek, yapay zeka çözümlerini genişletmek ve satış dışındaki müşteri yönetimi süreçlerine yönelik yeni özellikler geliştirmek için kullanacağını açıkladı.
Dreamteam, 2025 yılında eski Freshworks yöneticileri Anand Venkatraman , Senthil Kanthaswamy ve Ramesh Parthasarathy tarafından kuruldu. ABD merkezli girişim, şirketlerin müşteri ilişkilerini ve satış süreçlerini yapay zeka ile yönetmesini sağlayan bir CRM platformu geliştiriyor. Geleneksel CRM sistemlerinde satış ekiplerinin müşteri görüşmelerini, e-postaları ve satış fırsatlarını sisteme manuel olarak kaydetmesi gerekiyor. Bu da ekiplerin önemli ölçüde zaman harcamasına neden oluyor.
Dreamteam, bu süreci otomatikleştirerek satış ekiplerinin iş yükünü azaltmayı hedefliyor. Platform, e-postalar, toplantılar ve müşteri görüşmelerinden elde edilen bilgileri otomatik olarak topluyor. Böylece müşteri kayıtları güncel tutulurken satış ekipleri de veri girişi yerine müşterilerle ilişkilerini geliştirmeye odaklanabiliyor.
Platformun merkezinde Company Brain adı verilen bir sistem bulunuyor. Bu sistem, müşteriyle yapılan görüşmelerden ve diğer iletişim kanallarından gelen bilgileri tek bir yerde topluyor. Yapay zeka ajanları ise potansiyel müşterileri araştırıyor, takip e-postaları hazırlıyor, toplantılar için gerekli bilgileri derliyor ve satış anlaşmalarında ortaya çıkabilecek riskleri belirliyor.
Dreamteam, satış süreçlerinin yanı sıra müşteri desteği, yeni müşterilerin sisteme adaptasyonu ve mevcut müşterilere ek ürün veya hizmet satışı gibi alanlara da odaklanıyor. Magic Apps özelliğiyle kullanıcılar, kod yazmadan yalnızca yazılı komutlar vererek kendi ihtiyaçlarına uygun uygulamalar ve gösterge panoları oluşturabiliyor.

Instagram , katlanabilir ekranlı iPhone Duo için geliştirdiği uygulamanın arayüzünde değişiklikler yapmaya hazırlanıyor. Instagram CEO'su Adam Mosseri , uygulamanın farklı ekran boyutlarına ve kullanım biçimlerine uyarlanmasının oldukça zorlayıcı olduğunu belirtti. Threads üzerinden açıklama yapan Mosseri, iPhone Duo'nun tasarımını ve kullanım detaylarını inceledikçe uygulamayı cihazın ekran yapısına uygun hale getirmenin kolay olmayacağı sonucuna vardığını söyledi.
Mosseri'ye göre Instagram, uzun ve dikey ekranlar düşünülerek tasarlandığı için iPhone Duo'nun alışılmış akıllı telefonlardan farklı olan form faktörüne uyum sağlamakta zorlanıyor. Cihaz, katlanmış durumdayken bile diğer akıllı telefonlara kıyasla daha geniş ve daha kısa bir ekran sunuyor. Bu farklılık, uygulamanın arayüzündeki bazı öğelerin yeniden konumlandırılmasını gerektiriyor.
Mosseri, özellikle Reels deneyiminde karşılaşılan bir soruna dikkat çekti. Bir kullanıcının, cihazın büyük ekranı açıkken dikey konumda Instagram kullanmanın daha iyi bir deneyim sunduğunu belirtmesi üzerine Mosseri, bu kullanım biçiminin Reels için en iyi seçenek olduğunu kabul etti. Bununla birlikte şirketin uygulamanın diğer ekran yönlerindeki deneyimini de iyileştirmek için çalıştığını ifade etti.
Mosseri'nin verdiği örneklerden biri, gezinme düğmeleri ile Reels etkileşim butonlarının aynı bölgede konumlanması. Telefon katlanmış durumdayken ekranın sağ tarafında bulunan gezinme düğmelerinin ergonomik açıdan mantıklı olduğunu belirten Mosseri, Reels videolarındaki Beğen , Yorum ve Paylaş butonlarının da aynı tarafta yer aldığını söyledi. Bu durumun ekranda üst üste iki buton grubu oluşturduğunu belirten Mosseri, mevcut yerleşimin kullanıcı deneyimi açısından iyi olmadığını ve yeniden değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini dile getirdi.
iPhone Duo için tasarlanan Instagram uygulaması, 23 Ekim'de dünya genelinde kullanıma sunulmuştu. Ancak uygulama, yayınlanmasının ardından özellikle arayüz tasarımı ve butonların konumlandırılması nedeniyle kullanıcıların eleştirileriyle karşılaştı. Mosseri'nin açıklamaları, Instagram'ın bu eleştirileri dikkate alarak uygulamanın yeni sürümlerinde arayüzü yeniden düzenleyebileceğine işaret ediyor.

AI agent takes unapproved actions even when laptop lid is closed and told not to.
Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.
Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent’s reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.”
The NewCore employees sent the gateway logs to Grok Bot support personnel and asked what was causing the bots to access accounts without prompting or approval. The support team’s reply indicated the behavior was by design and intended to allow the bots to proactively take actions on behalf of users. In other words, the unrequested and unlogged access attempts were a feature designed to make Grok Bot more useful by periodically checking in and finding tasks to perform before a user even asks. The proactive check-in is a feature of Cursor, the AI coding service SpaceXSI recently acquired.
“There is no bug to patch, which is exactly why this is worse than a bug,” Ido Hoorvitch, a NewCore security researcher, wrote in an email. “A vulnerability gets fixed. This is the product working as designed: an agent that holds your credentials, acts under your identity while you sleep, ignores the one refusal you can give it, and then tells you it did nothing.”
Hoorvitch said that Grok Bot provides minimal notification of the automatic “turns,” or the cycles that occur when an agent receives instructions or context, decides what to do, and calls whatever tools it chooses. The notice comes during onboarding when the bot says it keeps working while the user is away from the computer and connects to apps and uses them the way the user does.
“It reads like a welcome message and scrolls off the screen in under a minute,” Hoorvitch said. “Nobody is asked to consent to it. Nothing says the platform will start turns with no message from you, or that those turns will use your connectors.”
The researcher said that Grok Bot documentation notes that a primary bot checks in on its own, and a changelog mentions brief background wakes, but there is no mention that the check-ins “reach into your connected apps.” Further, once a check-in runs, there is no mention of it in the chat interface or in the chat history, and as already noted, prompts to stop check-ins don’t work. Hoorvitch said the bot “always asks before making changes,” but that applies only to events in which data or changes are written to an app.
NewCore contacted Grok Bot support on November 4. At the time, users had no way to turn off the automatic check-ins. Then, eight days later, Hoorvitch said, the Cursor dashboard, the administrative console behind Grok Bot, received an update. Under bot capabilities, a new toggle called proactive messages appeared. By default, it’s set to on. When a team admin sets it to off, bots no longer run check-ins on their own.
SpaceXSI representatives didn’t answer questions sent by email.

President Donald Trump inspects an honor guard after stepping off Air Force One, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila, Philippines. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption
MANILA, Philippines — President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, where he was scheduled to meet regional partners, talk trade, and seek a break from a series of setbacks at home, ranging from a major disruption to the U.S. aviation industry to a scandal that has shaken the global AI industry.
Manila, the Philippine capital, is Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and, according to Trump, potentially for a meeting with North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un.
The visit marks Trump's first travel abroad since his party suffered deep losses in midterm elections. The White House and stock market alike have been rattled by the departure of Jensen Huang from Nvidia last week after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. Beijing has said it was not involved.
As he descended the stairs from Air Force One, Trump pumped his fist. A child handed him small American and Philippine flags, which Trump waved and then swooped in big circular motions as he smiled. The U.S. president was greeted by a marching band playing "YMCA" while he walked to a waiting helicopter.
Trump's first hours in the Philippines will include all the reassuring optics from Washington's oldest treaty ally in Asia, including a cocktail reception and dinner with other world leaders, an intermission from some of the thorniest issues at home. He's being feted Tuesday night at a gala as the "guest of honor" at the annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
The ASEAN leaders have been working on a non-aggression pact with China in the contested waters of the South China Sea, a key global trade route. Confrontations have escalated in recent years, particularly between Chinese and Philippine coast guard and naval forces in disputed shoals.
First on Trump's agenda Tuesday is a meeting with the leaders of the Quad nations, comprising the U.S., Australia, India, and Japan that have aimed to counter China's influence in the Asia Pacific. It will be their first meeting since Trump returned to the White House last year.
Trump is then scheduled to sign a trade deal with Thailand, the type of agreement he has relished striking since launching a trade war last year buttressed by steep tariff threats.
The U.S. had announced a trade framework last October in which Thailand would remove tariffs on most American goods, as well as barriers for importing U.S. autos, food products and pharmaceutical drugs, according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative. At the time, the Trump administration said Thailand would also spend more than $18 billion on U.S. aircraft and buy U.S. farm goods and liquefied natural gas.
The U.S. Supreme Court overturned in February the 19% tariff that Trump placed on goods from Thailand. The administration sought replacement tariffs in July by levying a 12.5% tax on imports from Thailand for not taking steps to oppose the use of forced labor.
Before the gala dinner Tuesday night, Trump will participate in what's billed as a "special summit" with the ASEAN leaders, where they are expected to discuss efforts to deepen trade and security ties as well as the region's longstanding conflicts, including yearslong violence in Myanmar and escalating disputes in the South China Sea, which Beijing claims virtually in its entirety.
Washington rejects China's expansive claim in the waterway, and has repeatedly stated that it's obligated to defend the Philippines if Filipino forces come under an armed attack.
Demonstrators hold signs during a protest against U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit and related meetings in Manila, Philippines, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Firdia Linsawati/AP hide caption
About 1,500 left-wing protesters held a noisy rally in a downtown Manila square ahead of Trump's arrival, calling on Philippine leaders not to take their foreign policy cues from the U.S.
They waved red flags and held up a large streamer that read, "Resist U.S. war and plunder!" They planned to burn an effigy of Trump. Riot police with shields and wooden truncheons stood nearby.
"The Philippine government should not deal with such a loser so our call to the Marcos administration is to stop being a puppet of Donald Trump and to uphold an independent foreign policy for the Philippines," protest leader Teddy Casiño told The Associated Press at the Liwasang Bonifacio square, referring to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
On Wednesday, Trump is set to receive a red-carpet welcome and full military honors from Marcos Jr., followed by a state banquet as part of his visit to the Malacanang presidential palace. Trump and Marcos are expected to affirm their commitment to their countries' longstanding treaty alliance.
Officials are arranging a possible brief reunion in Malacanang with an old acquaintance — Imelda Marcos — if she's well enough and gets her doctors' nod.
Now 97 and using a wheelchair, the former jet set Philippine first lady and mother of the incumbent president partied in New York decades ago in her heyday as the controversial wife of a strongman leader, who was to be ousted in a pro-democracy 1986 "People Power" public uprising.
But the friendship with Trump endured, with Trump often asking Marcos Jr. and other Philippine officials: "How's Imelda?" Philippine Ambassador to Washington Jose Manuel Romualdez told The Associated Press.
"Personal connections are very important to him," Romualdez said.
When the Philippine leader met Trump in the White House last year, he carried a note from his mother that thanked the U.S. president for his strong backing of the Philippines. "President Trump was very happy and told Marcos, 'please say hello to your mother,'" according to Romualdez.
Trump is also expected to announce a series of commercial deals and investments in the aviation, defense, energy, and technology sectors, before heading to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

FILE - A freight train runs on rails of a railway link of the Crimean Bridge connecting Russian mainland and Crimean peninsula over the Kerch Strait not far from Kerch, Crimea, on Monday, July 17, 2023. AP Photo//AP hide caption
A Ukrainian drone and missile attack prepared over several weeks struck a vital Russian rail and road bridge to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, in a stunning blow after nearly five years of war.
Zelenskyy portrayed the "unprecedented" operation on the Kerch Bridge as a masterstroke, as Ukrainian forces gradually wore down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target with missiles and drones overnight.
He didn't detail the damage but unconfirmed media reports said that a span of the bridge collapsed in the attack, in what would be an embarrassing setback for Moscow.
The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that traffic across the bridge has been halted and urged people "to refrain from trips in the direction of the bridge." He didn't mention any damage.
The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory for Ukrainians.
Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people.
A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022.
U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.
Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Flamingo precision-guided missiles delivered the final blow, he said.
Russia's Investigative Committee said that the bridge was attacked by drones on both days and sustained damage. It didn't elaborate on the extent of the damage.
Zelenskyy noted that Russia has battered Ukrainian infrastructure, especially the power grid, every day.
"We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," he said.
Russian air defenses downed 1,441 drones during a second straight night of major Ukrainian attacks, Russia's Defense Ministry said Tuesday.
On Monday, Russia said that it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones in the highest number of interceptions it had reported so far during the war.
Elsewhere, authorities in Bashkortostan, a Russian region in the south of Russia's Ural Mountains, said that defenses repelled a "massive" drone attack on industrial zones of the cities of Ufa and Salavat. All plants there worked as usual, and no critical damage has been inflicted on them, officials said.
Independent news outlet Astra, however, reported a huge fire at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex, located nearly 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of the Ukrainian border. The complex has been attacked a number of times before.
In Moscow, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that around 800 drones flew toward the Moscow region overnight. Most were downed far away, and 321 were shot down as they approached the Russian capital.
Experts are inspecting Kyiv's North and South bridges, damaged in a Russian ballistic missile attack, to assess the extent of the destruction, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Tuesday morning.
Russian attacks damaged other infrastructure and started fires in four districts of the Ukrainian capital, officials said, as Moscow continues its campaign to make life difficult for Ukrainian civilians.
The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that its forces overnight carried out a major strike using land- and air-based precision weapons and drones on Ukraine's military industrial facilities, energy, transport and port infrastructure, as well as vessels used for Ukraine's armed forces.
Russian forces launched a combined attack on industrial facilities in three districts of the southern Ukraine region of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and wounding 18 others and leaving a large number of consumers in the region without power, said Mykhailo Semikin, head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration.
Meanwhile, the negotiating teams of Ukraine, the United States, and European partners held a working video call on Monday, during which they discussed the results of recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, and the agenda for the next stage of negotiations, said Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service.
"We aligned our positions and our next joint steps," Umerov said on Telegram following the conversation.
On the European side, representatives of France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Poland, NATO and the European Commission joined the conversation.
The United States was represented by envoys Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of U.S. forces in Europe, Umerov said.

Robert Pattinson 'ın yeni James Bond olarak seçilmesi, beklenmedik bir ismi yeniden gündeme getirdi: Donald Trump . Pattinson'ın geçmişteki kız arkadaşı Kristen Stewart'ın, 'Pamuk Prenses ve Avcı' filminin yönetmeni Rupert Sanders ile fotoğraflandığı 2012 tarihinde, Trump'a ait X platformu mesajları internette yeniden ortaya çıktı.
Pattinson ve Stewart o dönemde Hollywood'un en çok konuşulan çiftleri arasındaydı. Stewart'ın Sanders ile çekilmiş fotoğraflarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından Pattinson ile ilişkileri bozulmuştu. Şimdi, Trump'ın ABD Başkanı olmasından yıllar önce atılan mesajlar yeniden gündemde.
Trump, Pattinson'ın aldatıldığını söyleyerek, "Onu terk et" ve "Hiç yanılıyor muyum?" gibi mesajlarla konuyu takip etmişti. 18 Ekim 2012 tarihli mesajlarından birinde şöyle yazıyordu:
"Pattinson/Kristen Stewart buluşmamla ilgili birçok yanıt aldım. Yine aldatacak - %100 eminim - hiç yanılıyor muyum?"
"Stewart/Pattinson hakkında çok fazla tweet ve haber var. Bakın, önemli değil - ilişki asla eskisi gibi olmayacak. Kalıcı olarak bitti."
"Herkes Robert Pattinson'ın Kristen Stewart'ı terk etmesi gerektiği konusunda haklı olduğumu biliyor. Birkaç yıl sonra bana teşekkür edecek. Akıllı ol Robert."
Pattinson'ın dün yeni James Bond olarak seçildiğinin duyurulmasının ardından, Trump'ın X platformu mesajları yeniden gündeme taşınarak üzerine konuşuldu ve sosyal medyada esprili yorumlar yapıldı. Özellikle Trump'ın, "Birkaç yıl sonra bana teşekkür edecek" sözleri James Bond olmasına yoruldu ve "Trump bildi" şeklinde eğlenceli mesajlar paylaşıldı.
İkonik casus serisini çekecek olan Amazon MGM Studios, dün '007' kod adlı İngiliz ajanı rolünün 40 yaşındaki Pattinson'a verildiğini açıkladı. Bu hamle, rolü üst üste beş kez canlandıran Daniel Craig'den bayrağı devralacak isim konusunda yıllardır süregelen spekülasyonlara son verdi. Craig, bir zamanlar alışılmadık bir seçim olarak görülse de, serinin zirvelere taşınmasına yardımcı olmuştu.
25 James Bond filminde altı farklı aktör, ajan rolünü canlandırdı. Jean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan ve Daniel Craig'den sonra James Bond rolünü üstlenecek yedinci oyuncu olan Pattinson, heyecanını şu sözlerle paylaştı:
“007 rolünün bana emanet edilmesi hayatımın en büyük onuru. Bana güvendikleri için Denis, Amy, David, Tanya ve Amazon MGM Studios'taki herkese minnettarım. Bu rolün bir hayalin gerçekleşmesi olduğunu söylemek bile yaşadığım heyecanı anlatmaya yetmez. Bu işbirliğinden ve böylesine harika bir ekiple çalışacak olmaktan dolayı büyük heyecan duyuyorum.”

Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’
Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.
The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.
Miliband announced the measures just before tenders for the large E1 West Bank settlement were due to be allocated by the Israeli government, while saying he wanted to work with a new Israeli government in a more cooperative way.
Israel’s possible new prime minister, Gadi Eisenkot has said that, if appointed, he will take a tougher approach than Benjamin Netanyahu to settler violence.
The sanctions are designed to stop the flow of finance to eight identified construction firms, although in practice the extent to which any of the firms are dependent on British finance is yet to be tested.
On 8 September, Miliband announced an expansion of its Global Human Rights sanctions regime, as well as a complex set of measures, yet to be implemented, designed to ban the trade in goods from illegal settlements. The Foreign Office said that it welcomed and encouraged trade with “green line Israel” and firmly distinguished this with activity in settlements.
The Foreign Office said the current Israeli government had “not only refused to clamp down on illegal settlement, but has facilitated and encouraged them”. More settlements had been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years.
The entities targeted by sanctions are Israeli construction, property development and architectural businesses that have helped to plan, build, supply or market housing and public infrastructure in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Miliband – who was criticised by some for broadening the sanctions criteria and planning a ban on trade with illegal settlement – said: “Protecting the two-state solution is the north star of this government’s approach.
“That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution. And we will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza. The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.”
But he added in a potential olive branch: “We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike.”
Miliband and his Middle East minister, Stephen Doughty, have repeatedly highlighted the Israeli government’s refusal to let a variety of dual-use goods into Gaza. The Foreign Office said civilians in Gaza were in desperate need of winter supplies, with catastrophic floods leaving nearly 4,000 households without shelter and 1.4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters.
According to the UN, more than 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins bought by humanitarian partners and donors are outside Gaza ready to go in, but are being held by the Israeli authorities. The Israeli authorities also continue to block timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza.
The Israeli government claims the blockage of some goods is necessary to prevent Hamas obtaining items that could be used to attack Israel. The dispute over dual-use goods and closed entry points into Gaza has lasted for more than two years.

A funeral was held for Fadwa al-Fahidat in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Tuesday
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.
There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.
According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.
There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.
They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.
Medics say Palestinians and Israelis were wounded in the incident on Monday evening
Palestinian reports said Fadwa al-Fahidat, who was 72, was shot outside her home on Monday evening and that, hearing the news, her son sped to the scene in his car.
He then collided with an empty Israeli vehicle parked outside his family home and settlers standing nearby were injured, they said. The settlers then began shooting, the reports said.
The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle".
Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat."
The IDF said that Israeli security forces were sent to the scene and were pursuing suspects.
Doctors at a hospital in Jericho said that al-Fahidat was shot in the head. Several other Palestinians and Israelis were injured, reports said.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement.
Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents.
A group of settlers set up a new outpost in al-Duyuk al-Tahta earlier this month (file photo)
In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent.
The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident.
Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now.
It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank".
The UK government said on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable.
