Izzy Goodwin has scored three goals in five WSL appearances for London City
London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin has been named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine.
The 23-year-old has been in great form this month and scored in front of England manager Sarina Wiegman at Emirates Stadium on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.
"We have always seen her as a huge talent with potential," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"I think London City are developing really well in the games they have showed. She is tall and can head a ball attacking-wise, but also defending.
"She is really quick with her feet and can score goals. I really want to see her in our environment, what she can bring and how close she is to the level that we expect."
There is also a first call-up for goalkeeper Katie Cox, on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea, while Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone returns.
Manchester City duo Niamh Charles and Alex Greenwood, who is injured, are among those to miss out.
The Lionesses play Ukraine in Spain on 1 December before hosting them at Wembley on 5 December. The winner qualifies for next year's Women's World Cup.
"We know what's at stake in these games and our focus is on producing two strong performances to secure our place at the World Cup," said Wiegman.
"We have worked hard to put ourselves in this position and now we have to finish the job.
"Ukraine will provide a challenge and we will prepare with the same focus and determination that we always do."
Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze could make her 150th appearance at Wembley in the second leg.
England travel to Pinatar, Spain a few days before the first leg and opted not to play a friendly match during this extended international break.
"The first part of the block we are [at St George's Park]. We have training sessions and a period of time where we can do some tactical stuff," added Wiegman.
"We also selected more players so that helps us create situations where we can train things and everyone is important. I'm really excited to get ready for these games."
Sarina Wiegman led England to victory at Euro 2022 and Euro 2025
Wiegman was speaking to media at St George's Park for the first time since signing a new contract that will run until the end of Euro 2029.
It means she could oversee England's fortunes at next year's World Cup if they beat Ukraine, as well as heading up a Team GB squad at the 2028 Olympic Games.
Asked why she wanted to extend her stay, Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Well, first of all the FA is happy with me and I'm really happy with them.
"I'm really grateful for that environment. That is one [reason]. Secondly, I still feel a great connection with staff and players, and of course the country!
"Then we have the challenges ahead. The major tournaments always motivate me. You don't get many moments with the team because it's not like it is at a club.
"In a tournament, you have those moments where you are really together, you can get somewhere with the group and that really excites me.
"Yes, the Olympics would be really great. Next year it's the World Cup, then it's the Olympics, then it's the Euros – that journey ahead really excites me."
Wiegman's contract renewal was kept under wraps and it came as a surprise following their two-legged victory over Greece in October.
The Dutchwoman, who has guided England to successive European titles, said conversations had been ongoing for a while but she had not planned ahead.
"When I signed that first contract in 2020 to join in 2021, it was a four-year contract and I thought, 'ok, this is a long contract, it would be really great if things go well'.
"We all got so excited so I signed another contract until 2027 and now I have until 2029. That is eight years. I never expected that. I also never planned so far ahead.
"I want to feel that I can contribute to the environment and the development of things. I also want that from the other party. You want it to fit and for it to work.
"That decision came over time. At one point you think: 'Yeah, I'm getting really excited again.' That is what you want. To feel the energy, to feel the excitement.
"I still think we have things we can improve. We know the game is improving so quickly so we have to adapt all the time. When you stand still, you are lost."
Wiegman is also determined to improve as a coach and has enjoyed overseeing the development of younger talent as the Lionesses transition.
"It starts with me and about how I am going to develop. I keep learning things about myself too. You need to know yourself really well to do this job," she added.
"The staff and the players will always challenge me in the right ways. It goes back and forth. That is what I want. I really want to improve myself all the time."

Sarina Wiegman says the potential in England’s emerging young players helped convince her to extend her contract until the end of 2029’s European Championship.
The Lionesses head coach, whose previous deal was due to expire next year, gave first senior call-ups to the striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox on Tuesday as she named her squad for December’s two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine.
Speaking to the media for the first time since signed her new contract in October, Wiegman described the Football Association as “a trailblazer with the women’s game and a great federation to work for” and said: “I’m really happy with the team but also talents coming through, which is exciting, and there’s now some high potential, and hopefully these talents go from high potential to world-class players, if not already. And I hope to have a part in that, too, and have a contribution to that. While I’m talking about that, I’m getting excited.
“The majority of their development is happening [at their clubs] but when they come to our environment, I hope to have a little part of that contribution.”
The Dutchwoman has led England to three consecutive major tournament finals, lifting two European titles, since taking charge in 2021 on a deal to 2025. Asked whether she had expected that to become an eight-year stay, she said: “No. I thought: ‘Four years, that’s a long time.’ Then it became six years and that looks like it’s becoming eight years. I would never have expected all of the things that we have reached.”
Will she call it a day in 2029? “Well, I tend to think that’s the end point, but you never know! I don’t plan that far ahead. So let’s see where it gets to.”

Wiegman, whose latest 25-player squad includes 10 players with fewer than 10 caps, watched from the stands at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday as Goodwin scored for London City Lionesses with a terrific finish against Arsenal. She said of the 23-year-old: “We always knew she’s a huge talent [with] a high potential. We’re watching a lot of games over periods of time, all the time, so we [had] kept an eye on her anyway, but I think it also helped that she had that great goal and a great performance last Sunday.
“She has some different qualities. She’s really fast too. She can head – she showed that also in attacking set plays and defending set plays also – and she can score goals. Does she need to step up to the next level? Absolutely. But you can tell that she’s improving.”
Wiegman was unable to call upon several injured players, including Lauren James and Alex Greenwood. She included Manchester United’s Ella Toone, who was initially left out of September’s squad before being recalled for the playoff against Greece. Wiegman said of Toone: “She has impressed us really well. She responded really well. And going back to [her] club, she’s done well too. And that’s what has been fed back to me too.”
Cox is rare in getting an England call-up while playing in the second-tier WSL2. The 20-year-old is on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea.
The Lionesses face Ukraine on neutral territory in Spain in the away leg on 1 December before playing them at Wembley four days later.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues.
The 62-year-old returned to football at West Brom last year following his recovery from bowel cancer, before taking charge at Blackburn in June.
In a statement, Mowbray said: "Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers.
"I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them.
"Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you.
"To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.
"I'm grateful to the owners and Suhail [Shaikh, Blackburn's chief operating officer] for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.
"I'd ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time.
Mowbray had enjoyed an impressive start to his second spell at Blackburn. Tipped for relegation by many, Rovers currently sit just three points off the play-offs in 13th. In their last game before the international break they beat West Ham 2-1.
Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will take charge of first-team affairs heading into Sunday's game with Burnley.

Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool
Vitor Matos is close to leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg.
Strasbourg have made an official approach for the Swansea head coach, who looks likely to depart even though there is no agreement yet between the clubs over a compensation package.
Matos was at Swansea's training ground on Tuesday morning, but is understood to have told the Championship side he wants to leave.
Matos is under contract until 2030, meaning Swansea will be due significant compensation should he depart.
But that has not stopped Strasbourg targeting the 38-year-old Portuguese, who had been due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month.
Current Strasbourg boss Hugo Oliveira, Matos' fellow countryman, is under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches.
Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to take over at Ipswich Town – in July.
O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone.
Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea.
Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November.
The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign.
Vitor Matos led Swansea to seven wins in their first 10 league games of the season, though they have since lost four in five
Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, enjoying two spells on top of the table, but their form has dipped in recent weeks.
Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot going into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion.
Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.
When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."
In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned.
"The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch," Gorringe said.
"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.
"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."
After West Brom visit, Swansea go to second-placed Middlesbrough next Tuesday before Cardiff City make the short trip west for the first south Wales derby in two seasons on Sunday, 29 November.
Should Matos depart, it is thought likely that a number of his backroom team will also move on.
Vitor Matos latest: Strasbourg close in on Swansea head coach
Vitor Matos is relatively inexperienced, if you look at his senior management experience alone, but his wealth of footballing experience is evident when taking a wider look at his footballing journey.
Speaking to BBC Sport earlier this season, Matos explained how his 23 years in football have informed his development - a journey that began when a 15-year-old Matos was inspired by Jose Mourinho's Champions League triumph with Porto.
So, although he only took his first managerial job at the start of last season in the second division of Portugal, to call Matos an overnight success story would be false.
He developed an understanding of positional play while working as a youth coach at FC Porto, before moving to China. As technical director and an under-16 coach of Shandong Taishan, he added layers of knowledge to his positional game:
"In China, I understood that to arrive at a more positional game, you could have different steps beforehand," he explained.
"There is a benefit to having more players close to each other, rather than spreading them over space.
"If you spread them over space, you are demanding that, technically, they can solve many situations one-v-one. If they come closer to the ball, you can generate more possibilities. You can create a tempo that allows other players to be better in the big spaces."
The uniqueness of these overloads, around the ball, have been a hallmark of some of Swansea's impressive attacking play this season.
Following stints in Portugal and China, he then found himself working alongside Jurgen Klopp and Pep Lijnders at Liverpool, which provided him a greater understanding of senior football at the elite level.
"Liverpool influenced me a lot in terms of counter-pressing, pressing, intensity, and what makes you grow as a team," he said.
"The most important thing is how much you believe in your idea, and this style is how I see football. That's why I want this to be the foundation for our team."

As Zeki Amdouni arrowed in second-string Switzerland's fabulous fourth goal, the body language of dejected Scotland duo Andy Robertson and Ryan Christie was telling.
The captain's record-breaking 103rd cap played out in cruel fashion. Suited and booted for the occasion, with commemorative boots and a personalised armband, there was no cause for celebration as Robertson was, yet again, wheeled out afterwards to make sense of the 4-0 scudding in St Gallen.
So too were John McGinn and Kieran Tierney. Billy Gilmour, who has also surpassed the half-century caps landmark, also did a bit of talking. Substitute Christie was spared this time.
After a result of this kind, rounding up a humdrum maiden campaign for manager Sebastien Pocognoli, it's necessary for the experienced heads to front-up.
When he named his first squad, so much kudos was thrown the Belgian's way for breaking away from the norm and bleeding in the stars of tomorrow.
But such young and bright lights were only allowed to shine on the bench, at best, as Pocognoli turned to the tried and tested.
As former Scotland international Leanne Crichton said on BBC Scotland's Sportscene: "There's a reliance still, clearly, on that key core of Scotland players.
"And, when you listen to it post-match, they sound dejected, they don't sound that confident about what is going on. It is a difficult place to be."
Pocognoli's abject Scotland suffer 4-0 Nations League defeat in Switzerland
St Gallen was a mighty troubling place for the Scots on Monday night.
The calm, picturesque city was invaded by coral shirt and kilt-clad Scotsmen from Sunday, but they - and their heroes on the pitch - couldn't wait to get out of the place after a poor showing at the Sitterstadion.
A narrow half-time deficit turned into a drubbing on the final whistle, at which the Scots remained goalless despite a handful of hopeful situations.
McGinn, the scorer of Scotland's past three goals, directed a weak header goalbound before the break, while Scott McTominay - nearly one year on from his Hampden heroics against Denmark - missed a couple of glaring opportunities.
"If McTominay is not operating at his highest level for the national team, there is an impact on results," Crichton said.
"If McGinn doesn't produce the goods on an evening, we're in trouble.
"If Gilmour and Ferguson in the middle of the pitch [don't perform], if Christie doesn't come on with an impact, we are [too reliant].
"And that's where you need to breed a different confidence in a different group."
Kieron Bowie, who many hoped would be in from the off, came on just before the hour mark and got right in about it, as is the striker's style.
Winger Ben Gannon-Doak, dropped for Aaron Hickey, did come on after the wing-back ended up going off with an apparent hamstring injury before Kristi Montgomery was handed a debut with five minutes to go.
Wide-men Findlay Curtis and Josh McPake were left on the bench, again. Robbie Ure didn't make either matchday squad this camp.
All three natural wingers excite supporters, even if they have only been handed a matter of minutes, but Pocognoli's system does not suit them.
That said, the players insist they're invested in the project.
"We have to believe that we're going in the right direction," Robertson added after a beyond-deflating defeat.
"Of course, there's going to be humps in the road, but when I look back on Steve Clarke's opening six games - I can't remember all the results but - I don't think everyone was shouting and screaming about Steve Clarke's Scotland after the first six games.
"We're trying to get a team together and we're trying to build a good atmosphere off the pitch.
"People wanted change within the squad. We've done that change and now we need to try and integrate the squad.
"We need to get close as a squad again, integrate the young players, make them feel a part of it, make them step up - it's for us to try and help them do it."
Pocognoli wants patience but Scotland 'don't have time' says Robertson

The statement is enough to make any Scotland fan uncomfortable, but that's been the relaxed theme going into this Nations League campaign among some outside of Hampden.
Euro 2028 has various different access routes, especially for the host nations of England, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, who even have two spare spaces between them secured before a ball is kicked.
But, in the bleak, barren and grim aftermath of Scotland's 4-0 scudding by Switzerland in St Gallen, "almost impossible" almost feels like a challenge.
Scotland began with three shots at reaching the finals, where they would play at Hampden Park if they made it. We're now down to two.
They could have qualified for the Euro 2028 finals with help from the Nations League. Not straightforward, but absolutely achievable.
Finish top of group B1 containing Switzerland, Slovenia and North Macedonia, then prevail in the play-off.
In Sebastien Pocognoli's first six games in charge, he failed to deliver that, his new-look squad and system only offering seven points.
Not only that but that third-place finish has further repercussions.
Scotland's next route lies in the Euro qualifiers, with the draw taking place in Belfast on 6 December. Can't wait.
Pocognoli's team will go into pot three for that, making a shot at progression that much more difficult.
That means the Scots could be drawn in a group with the likes of Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, or Austria as their pot 2 opponent.
For example, Scotland could be in a group with Spain, Switzerland, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan. Please, no.
The top 12 group winners and the eight best runners-up go straight through, with the rest of the runners-up going into a play-off with the best Nations League non-qualified group winners.
Uefa is reserving two spots for the two best-ranked host nations who have not qualified after the completion of the qualifying group stage.
Going on the assumption England - who have just turned over world champions Spain - will qualify, that leaves Scotland, Wales and Ireland. Despite the qualifying draw being in Belfast, Northern Ireland aren't a host nation.
If one of them qualifies through other means, then happy days.
If they do not, then the Scots will need to hope they are not the lowest-ranked team among the three or they face being locked out of their own house party.

Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".
The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances.
But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , external , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby.
"When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life.
"This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise."
The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it".
"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added.
"I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well.
"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.
"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it."
Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.
He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017.
But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments.
"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added.
"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.
"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.
"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.
"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it."

Few would have predicted that Carlo Ancelotti would be facing the wrath of a Brazil legend just 18 months into his tenure as head coach of the Brazil national team.
But Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo, has publicly demanded that legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties not once but twice in the last week alone.
It all started after Brazil suffered a 3-2 friendly defeat by Japan on Friday thanks to a controversial stoppage-time winner from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.
Ancelotti received a red card for dissent in the aftermath - the first of his international management career, as Barcelona forward Raphinha also saw red.
And in the wake of that defeat, despite it being a friendly, Romario quickly took to social media to air his frustrations about the former Real Madrid boss.
"Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and leave!" he wrote on Instagram.
"Nobody questions your history. You are one of the greatest coaches world football has ever seen, but that was at club level."
Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, a result which ensured they failed to qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time since 1990.
And Romario alluded to this too, stating that the country "can't take the risk of throwing another World Cup in the trash - the time to act is now!"
The Brazil boss has been in the game long enough to know how to deal with all sorts of opinions.
He has won the Champions League a record five times as a head coach and won the league title in all of Europe's top five divisions, along with multiple domestic cups.
But his record with Brazil is far from perfect. Across 21 matches, they have recorded 12 wins, four draws and five defeats.
However, while Ancelotti acknowledges the need for improvement, he emphasised the fact that it is still "a new project."
Speaking before Brazil's friendly with Singapore on Tuesday the Italian said: "In a democratic country with freedom of speech, everyone is allowed to express their opinion.
"It's not up to me to say whether the things he says are correct, wrong or just stupid. The truth is that Romario talks a lot. A lot. It's his right."
Despite the criticism he has faced, Ancelotti feels Brazil are on the right track and who is to tell him otherwise when you look at his track record?
You would have thought that would have been enough to let it lie for the time being.
But before Brazil had even kicked a ball in their next friendly against Singapore, Romario was speaking out again.
The former striker, who is the ninth-highest goalscorer in football history with 784 goals, doubled down on his calls for Ancelotti to be sacked.
"I talk a lot because when it comes to the national team, I have size, weight and power of speech," Romario, 60, said.
"I do not speak to gain followers, I do not speak for people to like me. I speak my mind.
"I have worn this shirt for many years and I am pretty sure I was one of the ones that helped the little yellow be respected all over the world."
He said he respected Ancelotti but added he hadn't "added anything new" to the national side.
"We will find another coach who will do a better job than you. And I'm saying this to your face, not through a message, including to the president of the CBF, who is long overdue to fire you."
Brazil faced Singapore in their final match of 2026 on Tuesday and won 7-0 .
Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior, who has come under scrutiny of his own so far this season, scored a hat-trick within the opening 21 minutes while Bournemouth winger Rayan and Chelsea's Estevao were also on the scoresheet.
It's a result that may bring a pause to proceedings in this war of words for now. However, if this last seven days has proved anything, it's that this saga is likely far from over.

Real Madrid forması giyen milli futbolcumuz Arda Güler, hem kulüp hem de milli takım forması altında sergilediği performansla izleyenleri büyülemeye devam ediyor.
Eflatun-beyazlı kulübe bu sezon 14 maçta 11 gollük katkı (4 gol - 7 asist) sağlayan genç orta saha oyuncusu, A Milli Takım 'ın son oynadığı Fransa maçında da atılan tek golün hazırlayıcısı oldu.
Bir dönem dünya futboluna damgasını vuran Fransa Milli Takımı Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane de 21 yaşındaki maestronun performansına kayıtsız kalamamış ve maçın ardından, "Arda Güler çok, çok, çok iyi bir oyuncu!" övgüsünde bulunmuştu.
İspanyol gazetesi Marca da Zidane'ın bu sözlerini bugünkü kapağına "Zidane bile Arda'ya hayran kaldı. Türk dehası son 8 maçta 4 gol - 5 asist üretti" ifadeleriyle taşıdı.
🗞️ Marca gazetesi, Fransa Milli Takımı Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane'ın 🇹🇷 Arda Güler hakkındaki sözlerini kapağına taşıdı: 💬 "Türk dehası, Real Madrid ve Milli Takım formasıyla çıktığı son 8 maçta 4 gol - 5 asist üretti. Zidane bile Arda Güler'e hayran kaldı: 'Çok, çok, çok iyi'"
Sahada her geçen gün daha da büyüyen ve sergilediği performansı sürekli olarak artıran Arda Güler, global ölçüde konuşulmaya devam ederken Real Madrid'e yakınlığıyla bilinen Defensa Central, ilginç bir istatistiğe dikkat çekerek milli futbolcunun Ballon d'Or'a göz kırptığını duyurdu.
PEDRI 261 MAÇTA 65 GOL KATKISI, ARDA 126 MAÇTA 54 GOL KATKISI VERDİ!
2025 yılında Ballon d’Or’a aday gösterilen ve Barcelona orta sahasının belkemiği olarak görülen Pedri, bordo-mavili forma altında çıktığı 261 resmi maçta 29 gol ve 36 asist kaydetti.
Buna karşılık Arda Güler, 126 maçta 22 gol ve 32 asist üreterek toplam 54 gole doğrudan katkı verdi.
İstatistiksel gözden bakıldığında Arda Güler, Pedri’nin oynadığı maç sayısının yarısından da daha az maça çıkmasına rağmen İspanyol orta sahanın verdiği gol katkısına oldukça yaklaşmış oldu.
Başta PSG olmak üzere Avrupa'nın birçok devinin uğruna astronomik rakamları gözden çıkardığı milli futbolcunun gelişimini ve performansını bu düzeyde sürdürmesi hâlinde 2027 Ballon d'Or ödülüne aday gösterileceği, hatta ödülün favorilerinden biri olacağı aktarıldı.

İspanyol Marca gazetesi, Real Madrid'li milli futbolcu Arda Güler için 'kendi imparatorluğunu kuruyor' ifadesini kullandı. 21 yaşındaki yıldızın Uluslar Ligi'nde Fransa ve Belçika'ya karşı oynadığı maçlar, Fransa Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane'dan ve Kevin De Bruyne'den övgü dolu sözler getirdi. Marca, 17 Kasım tarihli kapağında da Zidane'ın Arda'ya teslim olduğunu duyurdu.
Salı günkü Marca kapağında Arda Güler 'in diz çöküp kollarını açtığı kare yer aldı. Manşet, Zidane'ın maç sonrası söylediği 'Çok, çok, çok iyi' sözüydü; sol tarafta ise 'Zidane bile Güler'e teslim oluyor' yazıyordu. Gazete, 'Türk dahi' olarak andığı Arda'nın Real Madrid ve milli takım formasıyla oynadığı son sekiz maçta 4 gol ve 5 asist yaptığını, yani toplam 9 gole doğrudan katkı verdiğini duyurdu.
Marca'nın 'imparatorluk' başlıklı değerlendirmesi Opta verilerine dayanıyor. Uluslar Ligi'nde 27 faul kazanan Arda bu alanda zirvede yer aldı. Şut sayısında (23) ikinci, gol yaratan aksiyonlarda (5) dördüncü sırada bulunan oyuncu, 114 başarılı pas, 13 başarılı çalım ve 47 kazanılan ikili mücadeleyle Türkiye'nin birçok kategoride en iyi rakamlarına imza attı.
Türkiye, 15 Kasım Pazar günü Bordeaux'da Fransa 'ya 2-1 yenildi. Fransa'nın golünü milli formayla ilk golünü atan Eli Junior Kroupi kaydetti. Arda'nın ikinci yarıda ağlara gönderdiği top, İsmail Yüksek'in pozisyondaki hareketi nedeniyle ofsayt gerekçesiyle iptal edildi.
Türkiye'nin tek golü 90. dakikada geldi: Arda'nın kullandığı kornerde Abdülkerim Bardakcı topu ağlara yolladı. Maçın ardından konuşan Fransa Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane, Arda için 'Çok, çok, çok iyi' dedi. Zidane ayrıca Türkiye'nin topa sahipken iyi oyun kurabilen bir takım olduğunu, topla buluştuğunda güçlü oyuncuları bulunduğunu vurguladı.
İzmir 'de oynanan Belçika maçında Türkiye'yi 20. dakikada öne geçiren isim Arda'ydı; serbest vuruştan attığı gol Avrupa basınında geniş yer buldu. Belçika ise 27. dakikada Kevin De Bruyne ve 30. dakikada Charles De Ketelaere'nin golleriyle maçı 2-1 kazandı.
Maçın ardından konuşan De Bruyne, rakibine övgüler yağdırdı: ' Arda Güler muhteşem bir futbolcu. Dünyanın en iyi kulüplerinden birinde ve dünyanın en iyi futbolcularından biri.' Belçikalı yıldız, planlarını büyük oranda Arda'ya göre yaptıklarını da söyledi. Türkiye ise Uluslar Ligi'ni hiç puan alamadan tamamladı.

Scotland ended their Nations League campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Switzerland; Sebastien Pocognoli has won two of his first six games as head coach; the Scots are set to find themselves in pot three for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw
A year is a long time in football and that is certainly the case when it comes to Scotland's fortunes.
From a historic night against Denmark as the long wait to return to the World Cup finally ended, to a bruising 4-0 defeat to Switzerland at the end of a frustrating Nations League campaign. The contrast is stark.
A second-half collapse against a second-string Swiss side in St Gallen condemned the Scots to their heaviest loss since their 5-1 thrashing by Germany at Euro 2024.
After also leading Scotland to back-to-back Euros, Steve Clarke was always going to be a hard act to follow. After just six games, some of the Tartan Army have already seen enough from Sebastien Pocognoli.
The new head coach managed two wins against North Macedonia in Group B1. The third-place finish means Scotland will be in pot three when the qualifying draw is made for Euro 2028 on December 6, meaning a potentially more challenging campaign.
Pocognoli wants time, something even his captain Andy Robertson said you do not get in international football.
Pocognoli has consistently stressed the need for patience as he tries to implement a more attack-minded style.
He favours a back three featuring wing-backs, with two attacking midfielders or a central playmaker supporting a single striker as he looks to press high up the pitch.
Pacy winger Ben Gannon-Doak has frequently been deployed at right wing-back in this system, but his natural attacking fair is being limited by the defensive demands that brings.
While Clarke did use a back five in his early tenure to try and accomodate both Andy Roberston and John McGinn, he favoured a more traditional back four.
His teams were not always entertaining to watch, but they did get the job done. Most of the time.
The question for Pocognoli is, should he stick to his principles or look at what his predecessor did to bring the highs the Tartan Army had been missing?
After two camps and six games, any grace period the Belgian had is over.
Time with the players is something international managers do not have, but Pocognoli has already had more than some.
The elongated international window between September and October, followed by the most recent camp means he has had 24 days with his squad. That is equivalent to what a Scottish Premiership side has between day one of pre-season and their first game in the League Cup group stages.
Andy Robertson became Scotland's most capped men's player against Switzerland, but there was not much for the captain to celebrate.
"That cannot happen in international football," he told BBC Scotland after the match.
"I don't think you've got time in international football, you have to do it. These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden, who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.
"We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up."
John McGinn echoed his skipper when asked if Scotland were on the right path: "Well, obviously the trajectory of the results means it's impossible for me to say yes."
James Scott from the Football Park Scotland podcast speaking on Sky Sports News:
"It's the early days and the players. It'll take time for us to maybe get going on this but that can't be the detriment of results.
"We can accept a poor performance against Macedonia, still getting the win, but coming away against Switzerland, it's a much tougher task and I think we could save face a bit by maybe just making a few adjustments.
"Losing against Switzerland is not a bad thing but to ship four goals in the manner we did with the lack of fight, the jury's out on the formation now. It's starting to frustrate people.
"We've got two friendlies now in March, Euro qualifiers starting next year. If things don't change in the friendlies, the frustration really will start to build because you don't get a lot of time in international football and I think mistakes do cost you more.
"We can't make amends for last night until then and then the qualifiers come around and there's really no room to slip up there because you don't want to be relying on the sort of safety net of being a host to get in.
"We would like to qualify and we don't want to miss out on a tournament that's happening in our own back garden and not being there."
The next international break is not until March, with two friendlies before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign kicks off.
Robertson admitted the long wait is "not a good thing" as they look to regroup after the Nations League disappointment.
While that means no time on the pitch with his players, Pocognoli will have time to assess his squad and tactics. If the Scottish FA decides he is still the right man to lead the national team to their next major tournament.

Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan, Ankara'da Suriye Dışişleri Bakanı Esad Hasan Şeybani ile ortak basın toplantısı düzenliyor.
Akkuyu Nükleer Güç Santrali'nin (NGS) ilk reaktöründe fiziksel çalıştırma hazırlıkları sürerken, yaklaşık 7 yıl Rusya'da eğitim gören Türk mühendisler Mehmet Zahid Akın ve Harun Burak Özdemir, meslek hayatlarının ilk yıllarında görev aldıkları projede emeklerinin karşılığını görmenin heyecanını yaşıyor.
Akın'ın iş günü, montaj belgelerini incelediği masa ile montajı yerinde kontrol ettiği saha arasında geçiyor. Özdemir ise son aylarda ekibiyle birlikte ilk ünitenin reaktör binasının koruma kabına yönelik sızdırmazlık ve dayanıklılık testlerini 29 Ekim Cumhuriyet Bayramı'na kadar tamamlamak için çalıştı.
Antalya'da düzenlenen Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi 31. Taraflar Konferansı (COP31) kapsamındaki "Dünya Nükleer Günleri" etkinliğinde AA muhabirine değerlendirmede bulunan iki mühendis, yaklaşık 4,5 yıldır Akkuyu NGS'de çalışıyor.
Akkuyu NGS'nin ilk reaktöründe fiziksel çalıştırmanın birkaç hafta içinde yapılması bekleniyor. Bu süreçte reaktörde ilk kez kontrollü zincirleme reaksiyonun sağlanması hedefleniyor.
Akkuyu Nükleer AŞ Yardımcı Sistemler Bölümü Montajdan Sorumlu Kıdemli Uzmanı Akın, Rusya'ya gitmeden önce biraz korktuğunu ancak bu duygunun zamanla yerini merak ve umuda bıraktığını söyledi.
Yaklaşık 7 yıl boyunca Rusça nükleer mühendislik eğitimi aldıklarını aktaran Akın, "Türkiye'nin ilk nükleer santralinde çalışacak ilk nükleer mühendislerden olmak ayrı bir gurur verdi. O korku da zamanla tamamen kayboldu." dedi.
Akın, ekibiyle birlikte yardımcı sistemlerin montaj sürecini satın alma aşamasından işin tamamlanmasına kadar takip ettiklerini, mevzuata uygunluğu ve kalite kontrol belgelerini incelediklerini anlattı.
Sahadaki bir gününü, "Günüm genelde bilgisayar başında ve sahaya giderek, ikisinin arasında mekik dokuyarak geçiyor. Gerekli belgeleri kontrol ediyorum, yanıma alıyorum, sahaya gidiyorum, yerinde kontrol ediyorum, geliyorum, raporumu yazıyorum." sözleriyle özetleyen Akın, hazırlıklar ilerledikçe iş temposunun da arttığını dile getirdi.
Akın, yoğun tempoya ilişkin "Bu büyük projeye katkı veriyor olmak gerçekten insana büyük bir motivasyon ve enerji sağlıyor. O yüzden fiziksel yorgunluk geçer, sıkıntımız yok. Canla başla, hızlı bir şekilde bitirmek için çalışıyoruz." ifadelerini kullandı.
Akkuyu Nükleer AŞ Mühendislik ve Teknik Destek Bölümü Güvenlik Sistemleri Grubu Baş Uzmanı Özdemir de santralin personel yetiştirme programı kapsamında 2015'te Rusya'ya gittiğini söyledi.
Moskova Fizik Mühendisliği Enstitüsünden 2022'de onur derecesiyle mezun olan Özdemir, öğrenciliğinde bilimsel araştırma projelerinde yer aldı ve Rusya'da düzenlenen "Ben Profesyonelim" olimpiyatında nükleer mühendislik alanında bronz madalya kazandı. Aynı yıl Akkuyu NGS'de çalışmaya başlayan Özdemir, güvenlik sistemlerinin testlerinin planlanması, belgelenmesi ve sonuçlarının değerlendirilmesinde görev alıyor.
Özdemir, reaktör binasının koruma kabına yönelik sızdırmazlık ve dayanıklılık testlerini ekip olarak 29 Ekim Cumhuriyet Bayramı'na kadar tamamlama hedefi belirlediklerini anlattı.
Testleri başarıyla tamamladıklarını belirten Özdemir, "Biz bu işi 29 Ekim'e bitirebiliriz dedik. Hakikaten önümüze böyle bir hedef koyduk ve muvaffak olduk. Cumhuriyet'imizin 103'üncü yılına kendi adımıza biz de bir hediye verdik." dedi.
Özdemir, nükleer enerji alanını "geniş bir bilgi okyanusu" olarak tanımladı. Mesleğinin kendisine kazandırdığı düşünme biçimini günlük yaşamına da taşıdığını kaydeden Özdemir, "Ben hatta evde yemek pişirirken bile kullanıyorum." ifadesini kullandı.
Santralden şebekeye ilk elektriğin verilmesini heyecanla beklediğini anlatan Özdemir, "4,5 senedir verdiğim emeğin artık sonucunu alma, meyvelerini görme gibi bir heyecanı da içten içe yaşıyorum. Son derece mutluyum." diye konuştu.
Türkiye ile Rusya arasında imzalanan hükümetler arası anlaşma kapsamında yürütülen personel yetiştirme programıyla Akkuyu NGS'de görev alacak Türk uzmanlar yetiştiriliyor.
Akkuyu Nükleer AŞ'den edinilen bilgiye göre, program kapsamında 2011-2025 döneminde Rusya'daki üniversitelerden 322 Türk öğrenci mezun oldu. Halihazırda 131 Türk öğrencinin eğitimine devam ettiği programla, nükleer enerji ve ilgili uzmanlık alanlarında en az 600 Türk vatandaşının eğitim alması hedefleniyor.
Mezunlar, Akkuyu Nükleer AŞ'nin farklı teknik birimlerinde görev alıyor. Aralarında reaktör ve türbin operatörleri ile elektrik ekipmanlarının işletilmesinden sorumlu uzmanlar da bulunuyor.
Uzmanlar, göreve başlamadan önce Rusya'da faaliyetteki nükleer enerji santrallerinde ve Rosatom'un eğitim merkezlerinde uygulamalı eğitim ve staj yapıyor.

1999 yılında Magazin Gazetecileri Derneği'nin ödül töreninde Ahmet Kaya 'ya yönelik gerçekleştirilen protesto, yıllar geçmesine rağmen tartışılmaya devam ediyor. O gece 10. Yıl Marşı'na eşlik ettiği için eleştirilen şarkıcı Mahsun Kırmızıgül, yaptığı son açıklamayla yeniden gündeme geldi.
Kırmızıgül, o gece ayağa kalkmasının Ahmet Kaya 'ya tepki göstermek amacı taşımadığını belirterek yaşananları farklı bir açıdan değerlendirdi. Salonda ayağa kalkmaması halinde kendisinin de ağır tepkilerle karşılaşabileceğini söyleyen Kırmızıgül, "O salonda ayağa kalkmasaydım başıma neler geleceğini, nasıl bir linçle karşı karşıya kalacağımı bugün bile düşünemiyorum" dedi.
Ahmet Kaya 'nın Türkiye'den ayrılmasına neden olan sürecin sorumluluğunun yalnızca o gece salonda bulunan kişilere yüklenemeyeceğini savunan Kırmızıgül, asıl sorumluluğun dönemin medyası ve siyasi atmosferinde olduğunu ifade etti. Kaya ile arasında yaşanan kırgınlığa da değinen ünlü şarkıcı, yeniden görüşmek için Almanya'ya gitmeyi düşündüğünü ancak Kaya'nın bir konserinde söylediği iddia edilen sözleri duyduktan sonra bu kararından vazgeçtiğini anlattı. Bu kararından dolayı pişmanlık duyduğunu belirten Kırmızıgül, "Keşke gitseydim. Keşke oturup konuşsaydık. Keşke birbirimizi dinleyebilseydik" ifadelerini kullandı.
Ahmet Kaya 'nın vefatının ardından Paris'e giderek mezarı başında vedalaştığını söyleyen Kırmızıgül, hakkındaki eleştirilere ise şu sözlerle yanıt verdi: "Ben hiçbir zaman Ahmet Kaya 'ya düşman olmadım. Onu protesto etmedim. Ona yapılan saldırının ve linçin hiçbir zaman parçası olmadım."
Kırmızıgül'ün son açıklamalarının ardından, yıllar önce Reha Muhtar'ın programına konuk olduğu sırada Ahmet Kaya hakkında yaptığı değerlendirmeler de yeniden gündeme geldi. Programda yaşananları "Yanlış bir geceydi" sözleriyle değerlendiren Kırmızıgül, Ahmet Kaya'nın açıklamalarına ilişkin dikkat çeken ifadeler kullanmıştı. Kırmızıgül, o programda, "Yanlış bir geceydi. O gece bunların olmaması gerekirdi. Ahmet Kaya, söylediklerini farklı bir dille söylese bugün böyle olmayabilirdi. Kürtçe zaten şu anda serbest... Binlerce Kürtçe kaset var" demişti.

Declan Rice has agreed a new long term-contract at Arsenal so can he continue to go from strength to strength? Jack Wilshere, his former team-mate at West Ham, tells Sky Sports Rice is "definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world"
Arsenal's Kroenke family owners tend not to get involved in transfer dealings. But when it came to Declan Rice, and the prospect of spending £100m on a player for the first time, they needed to be sure that it was a sensible investment.
So, in the conference room at Arsenal's training ground, co-chair Josh Kroenke asked to be walked through the deal by Mikel Arteta, former sporting director Edu, then executive vice-chair Tim Lewis and now chief executive officer Richard Garlick.
"My eyebrows raised because I didn't know if we were in that phase just yet to go after a player like that," Kroenke recalled. He wanted to know what he would bring and how Arteta would use him.
Kroenke left the meeting in no doubt about the deal, either financially or in footballing terms. A club-record approach to West Ham was greenlit and Rice has of course gone on to prove an inspired addition, his new deal reflecting his importance.
"Declan Rice, we got him half price," is the refrain among Arsenal supporters. A player instrumental in their Premier League title success, who insisted "it's not done", then did more than anyone to drive them over the line, is now tied down for his peak years.
He has brought Arsenal even more than the club anticipated, arriving as a No 6 before being unshackled as a rampaging No 8, then reverting to a deeper role this season.
He scores, creates and dominates physically. His deadly set-piece delivery, honed to a world-class level, is another weapon.
"He is becoming a total player," said Arteta, who has even called on him at right-back. Of course, Rice filled in admirably in that role. "A total player has to be able to do as many things as possible and he has the capacity to do that," added Arteta.
Rice's adaptability and willingness to evolve his game have been themes of his time at Arsenal. The same traits were apparent to those who worked with him at West Ham, where he made an instant impression on his former team-mate Jack Wilshere.
"I love Declan, first of all a person," Wilshere tells Sky Sports. "I could see that straight away when I went in. He was very humble, his eyes were open, he wanted to learn, he would ask the right questions, and he just went from strength to strength.
"His footballing ability speaks for itself, but I wouldn't say he's someone who it came naturally to. He had to work on his right foot, on his left foot. But physically, he was always a beast and that would help him get out of certain situations."
Wilshere also noted the leadership qualities that have come to the fore at Arsenal. "Even when I went there and he was 19 or 20 and finding his way in the team, he had natural leadership and a natural aura about him that you could see," he says.

"He has a good understanding as well. When you look at players making big moves now, for me, one of the most important things around it is timing. I think Dec got his timing right.
"He spent a good few years at West Ham becoming a hero, becoming an important member of that team, trying to get that team up the table to finish high as possible. He won a trophy with them, and then he decided to go and compete for bigger things."
Wilshere and Rice crossed paths again following his move to Arsenal, where Wilshere, now head coach of Luton Town, was working as an academy coach and shadowing his old team-mate Arteta.
"I know how important he was to Mikel at that time when Mikel brought him in, and how he was going to be that shining light of the team who would always be present," he says.
"That's another thing that's really impressive about him: his robustness. He plays every single game. He dominates every single game physically."
Rice's record bears it out. Last season was his most demanding yet as he made 55 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal, many of them while managing hamstring nerve pain, before making a further eight for England at the World Cup during the summer.
He is an incredible athlete who continues to show remarkable resistance to injury. He has only missed five out of 119 Premier League games since his arrival at Arsenal. Only four outfield players have played more minutes in the competition in that timeframe.
His reliability is invaluable to Arteta and Rice continues to find ways to improve. Having moved back to the base of midfield this term, switching to the right side of the pivot to accommodate Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes, he has become notably more incisive with his passes.
His total of five assists is the highest of any Premier League player this season and it is notable that all of them have come in open-play.
According to Opta, Rice ranks second among Premier League players - and top among midfielders - for line-breaking passes this season, behind only Jan Paul van Hecke. He also ranks second only to Martin Odegaard for line-breaking passes in the final third.
A player once criticised for sideways passing is now averaging nearly twice as many line-breaking passes than last season, showing clear development in yet another area of his game.
The hope for Arsenal is that Rice will continue to unlock more levels after committing his future to the club. That is certainly the expectation from those who know him.
"I actually think there's more to come from Dec," adds Wilshere. "I've said it for a few years now. To be fair, he has started to add goals, but I still think he can add more with his physical ability, with his ability to strike the ball off his left foot, right foot.
"But he's already a top player and definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world."

Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan, Ankara'da Suriye Dışişleri Bakanı Esad Hasan Şeybani ile ortak basın toplantısı düzenliyor.
Kulüpler Birliği Vakfı Genel Sekreteri Çağrı İlk'in açılış konuşmasını gerçekleştirdiği zirvenin sabah seansında Polonya Birinci Futbol Ligi (Ekstraklasa) Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Marcin Animucki, Avrupa Kulüpler Birliği (EFC) Finans Direktörü Hugo Hamon ile Strateji ve Kulüp İlişkileri Direktörü Michael Verschueren sunum yaptı.
Bir otelde düzenlenen Futbol Zirvesi'ne Galatasaray Kulübü Başkanı Dursun Özbek, Fenerbahçe Kulübü Futbol Direktörü Oğuz Çetin, Göztepe Kulübü Onursal Başkanı Mehmet Sepil ile Avrupa ligleri ve Türk kulüplerinden çok sayıda temsilci de katıldı.
Zirvenin açılış konuşmasında, Türk futbolunun Avrupa'da çok daha etkin ve rekabetçi bir konuma ulaşmasını sağlamak adına dünyadaki başarılı uygulamaları yakından takip etmenin büyük önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Çağrı İlk, "Türk futbolu; köklü kulüpleri, rekabetçi yapısı, geniş taraftar kitlesi ve ticari potansiyeliyle Avrupa futbolunda önemli bir konumda bulunmaktadır. Aynı zamanda kısa vadeli çözümler yerine uzun vadeli ve sürdürülebilir bir bakış açısıyla hareket etmenin gerekli olduğunu düşünüyoruz." şeklinde konuştu.
Avrupa futbolunun önde gelen kurumlarını temsil eden, alanlarında önemli bilgi ve deneyime sahip değerli isimleri ağırlamaktan mutluluk duyduklarını aktaran Çağrı İlk, "Konuklarımız, lig yönetiminden finansal sürdürülebilirliğe, dijital yayıncılıktan küresel markalaşmaya ve oyun kurallarındaki yeniliklere kadar futbolun geleceğini şekillendiren önemli başlıklardaki bilgi ve deneyimlerini bizlerle paylaşacak. Kulüpler Birliği Vakfı olarak kulüplerimizin ortak menfaatlerini korumaya, uluslararası iş birlikteliklerini güçlendirmeye ve Türk futbolunun gelişimine katkı sağlamaya devam edeceğiz. Bu vesileyle davetimizi kabul ederek bizlerle birlikte olan tüm konuşmacılarımıza, katılımlarıyla organizasyonumuza değer katan kulüp temsilcilerimize, basın mensuplarımıza ve akademisyenlerimize içtenlikle teşekkür ediyorum." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Marcin Animucki ise zirvede yaptığı sunumda Ekstraklasa'nın yönetim şekli, sponsorluk, pazarlama, yayın hakları gibi konularda bilgilendirmede bulundu.
Ekstraklasa'nın 2005'teki kuruluşundan itibaren büyük değer kazandığını vurgulayan Animucki, "2019'da medya haklarında yüzde 60, pazarlama haklarında ise yüzde 100 artış sağladık. 2023-2024 ile 2026-2027 sezonları arasındaki yeni ihalede ise değeri yüzde 30 kadar artırdık. Nesillere yönelik yapılan anket çalışmalarında davranış kalıpları hakkında bilgi sahibi oluyoruz. Yeni nesiller için de yeni satış stratejileri geliştirmemiz gerekiyor. Gelecek 10 yıl içerisinde 3 ya da 4 yeni stat yaparak seyirci sayımızı yüzde yüz artırmayı hedefliyoruz. Türkiye, Polonya ve ABD, UEFA ve FIFA anketlerine göre en modern statlara sahip üç ülke. Yeni jenerasyonları statlara çekme konusunda heyecanlıyız. İzleyici sayısı arttıkça gelirlerin de arttığını görüyoruz." ifadelerini kullandı.
Ligin yayıncılık çalışmaları hakkında detaylar paylaşan Animucki, "Ekstraklasa karşılaşmaları için 5 binden fazla prodüksiyon ürettik. Yeni jenerasyonlar için önem taşıyacak 21 yıllık arşivimizi de çeşitli dijital platformlarla paylaşıyoruz. Maç yayınları sırasında haftanın 3 büyük müsabakasında 24-26 kamera, diğer 6 karşılaşmada ise 14-16 kamera kullanıyoruz. Yarı otomatik ofsayt sistemi için de 10-12 kameradan faydalanıyoruz." diye konuştu.
Polonya'daki stat zeminlerinin bakımı için yapılan çalışmalardan da bahseden Animucki, "2015'te kulüplerin zeminden sorumlu çalışanlarının yanında UEFA ve FIFA'dan bir görevli yetkilendirildi. Neticede her takım, stat ve şehrin iklimi farklı olduğu için bu yetkili kişi, tüm kulüpleri ziyaret ederek zemin çalışmaları için görüşmeler gerçekleştiriyor. Kulüplerden zeminlerin haftada 4-5 saatten fazla kullanılmamasını talep ediyoruz. Zeminlerin zarar görmemesi için konserlerin sezon sonrasında yapılmasını da istiyoruz." şeklinde görüş belirtti.
EFC Finans Direktörü Hugo Hamon ile Strateji ve Kulüp İlişkileri Direktörü Michael Verschueren, zirvede yaptıkları sunumda Türk kulüplerinin finansal profili ve potansiyelini ele aldı.
Türk kulüplerinin 2024-2025 sezonunda 878 milyon avro gelirle Avrupa'da 7. sırada olduğunu kaydeden Hamon, "Türkiye, güçlü markalar ve istisnai taraftar topluluğuna sahip büyük bir pazar. Bu göz önünde bulundurulduğunda maç günü gelirleri de büyük bir potansiyel barındırıyor. Sürdürülebilir finansal yapının sağlanması halinde Türk futbolunun önünde bu anlamda parlak bir gelecek olduğunu görebiliyoruz." yorumunu yaptı.
Dijital platformlarda Türkiye'nin büyük takipçi kitlesine sahip olduğunu aktaran Hugo Hamon, "Beşiktaş, Fenerbahçe, Galatasaray ve Trabzonspor'un Instagram takipçi sayısı, Hollanda, Belçika, İskoçya, Portekiz ve İsviçre gibi ülkelerdeki bazı önde gelen kulüplerin toplam takipçi sayısından fazla. Türkiye, profesyonel kulüp sayısında da dünya çapında ikinci, UEFA'da ilk sırada." diye konuştu.
Türkiye'de yayın geliri dağılımında geçmiş şampiyonluklara göre kulüplere verilen yüzde 11'lik payın ortadan kalktığını hatırlatan Hamon, kulüplerin 2026-2027 sezonundan itibaren dağılımın yüzde 48’ini eşit, yüzde 46’sını sezon içi performansına, yüzde 6’sını ise sezon sonu sıralamasına göre alacağını ifade etti.
Ayrıca Hamon, Türk kulüplerinin 2021-2022 sezonundan beri transfer harcamalarında 680,2 milyon avro zarar ettiğini de sözlerine ekledi.
EFC'nin yönetim yapısı ve çalışmalarından bahseden Michael Verschueren ise yönetim kurulunun 35 kişiden oluştuğunu ifade ederek Galatasaray Kulübü Başkanı Dursun Özbek'in Türk futbolunun çıkarlarını gözetmek amacıyla kurulda yer aldığını belirtti.
